Classes

MemoryKunCache

In-process IKunCache backed by
IMemoryCache. Stores values directly — no
serialization round-trip — so mutations on cached reference
types are visible to other consumers. Callers that care about
isolation should cache immutable records or value types.

RedisKunCache

Distributed IKunCache backed by an
IDistributedCache instance (typically
Microsoft.Extensions.Caching.StackExchangeRedis). Values are
serialized via the registered IKunCacheSerializer.

SystemTextJsonCacheSerializer

Default IKunCacheSerializer backed by
JsonSerializer. Uses web-style options (camelCase,
case-insensitive reads) and respects the caller's
JsonSerializerOptions when supplied.

Remarks

When KunCachingOptions.FallbackToMemoryOnRedisFailure = true,
connection / socket failures are swallowed and the operation is
routed to an in-memory sidecar cache for the duration of the
outage. The fallback is per-process; other replicas will not see
writes made while Redis is unreachable.

public interface ITenantProvisioner

Remarks

Shared 策略不需要具体实现 —— 新租户只是多一行 TenantId 的业务记录。消费者只需要注册
NullTenantProvisioner（或依赖框架提供的 Singleton 默认值）。

SchemaPerTenant 与 DatabasePerTenant 策略依赖本接口的非空实现：在租户开户时分别创建 schema
或独立数据库，并在该隔离容器内运行 EF Core migrations。实现必须是幂等的 ——
使用 CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS / CREATE DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS 语义；
重复调用不得产生副作用。

调用时机由业务方控制；框架不做自动编排。典型场景：租户 signup API 成功创建租户记录后，
同事务（或补偿事务）里调用 ITenantProvisioner.ProvisionAsync；租户注销走反向流程。

Namespace: Kun.Core.MultiTenancy

SaaS 多租户数据隔离策略。由 Kun.EntityFrameworkCore.MultiTenancy 层在运行时解析成
具体的 DbContext 构造、迁移调度与连接解析行为。

public enum TenantIsolationStrategy

Fields

DatabasePerTenant = 2

每租户独立数据库实例（通常也是独立连接字符串、独立备份、独立 RPO/RTO）。
适用：合规要求强（医疗/金融 GDPR 数据主权）、租户数量 <= 数百但单租户数据量大。

SchemaPerTenant = 1

同库不同 schema，每个租户有独立 schema。逻辑隔离更强、备份粒度到租户；需要运行时
按 ITenantContext.TenantId 切 DefaultSchema 与 MigrationsHistoryTable。
适用：合规要求中等（如数据可"单租户导出"）、租户数量 <= 数千。

Shared = 0

所有租户同库同 schema，用 IMultiTenant 实体的 TenantId 列 + 全局查询
过滤器做应用层隔离，叠加 PostgreSQL RLS（AddKunTenantRls()）做 defence-in-depth。
适用：租户数量大但单租户数据量小、合规要求普通的 B2B SaaS。

Remarks

Part 1（2026-04-23）只落地枚举本身 + 配套契约类型；TenantIsolationStrategy.SchemaPerTenant 与
TenantIsolationStrategy.DatabasePerTenant 的运行时实现分别延后到 P2-D Part 2 / Part 3。
详细取舍见 docs/architecture/adr-p2d-multitenancy.md。

Remarks

Each operation provides two delegate-shape overloads:

a sync-delegate variant (no CancellationToken)

an async-delegate variant that accepts a CancellationToken and forwards it to the delegate.

cancelled source tasks surface through await per normal

exception.

Remarks

These helpers compose count + page queries into a single PagedResult<T>.
Callers are expected to annotate their query methods with [DapperAot] so that
Dapper.AOT generates the reader code at build time. The helpers themselves only call
the standard Dapper SqlMapper extensions and introduce no runtime reflection.

Remarks

Also registers TenantRlsConnectionInterceptor as Scoped; it does not
activate unless the caller adds it to their DbContextOptionsBuilder via
opts.AddInterceptors(sp.GetRequiredService<TenantRlsConnectionInterceptor>()).

AddKunTenantRls(IServiceCollection)

兼容入口：注册 RLS 双拦截器；推荐使用泛型重载自动装配。Consumers must
also wire the interceptor into their DbContext options via DI resolution, e.g.

services.AddDbContext<CatalogDbContext>((sp, options) =>
    options.UseNpgsql(cs)
           .UseKunSchema("catalog")
           .AddInterceptors(sp.GetRequiredService<TenantRlsTransactionInterceptor>()));

Scoped lifetime — each request's ITenantContext
is resolved per transaction. Not added automatically because the interceptor fires a
set_config round-trip on every transaction; services without RLS should not pay
that cost.

TenantRlsConnectionInterceptor

into the PostgreSQL session variable app.current_tenant_id on every

filter remains the first line of defence; this interceptor is the second.

EF Core transaction so PostgreSQL Row-Level Security policies can use
current_setting('app.current_tenant_id') to enforce tenant isolation even when a
caller bypasses the global query filter (e.g. IgnoreQueryFilters(), admin scenarios).

Defence-in-depth interceptor that pushes the current ITenantContext.TenantId
into the PostgreSQL session variable app.current_tenant_id on every
connection open, and clears it on connection close. Used in combination with
Row-Level Security policies on the database side — EF Core's global query
filter remains the first line of defence; this interceptor is the second.

Remarks

Only activates when the underlying DbConnection is an Npgsql
connection; for other providers (MySQL, SQL Server) the interceptor is a
no-op, because the SET app.current_tenant_id = ... syntax is
PostgreSQL-specific. The check is nominal (namespace-prefix on the connection
type) so this module can remain free of a direct Npgsql package dependency.

SQL injection guard: SET statements in PostgreSQL cannot be parameterised,
so the tenant id is inlined into the command text. We therefore refuse to emit
the command unless the value matches the strict whitelist
TenantRlsConnectionInterceptor.SafeTenantIdPattern. A business tenant id that does not match
(spaces, quotes, semicolons, etc.) will throw instead of being silently coerced
— fail loudly rather than hand a crafted value to SET.

Registered as Scoped by KunEntityFrameworkCoreServiceCollectionExtensions.AddKunEntityFrameworkCore;
callers opt in by adding the interceptor to their DbContextOptionsBuilder:

services.AddDbContext<MyDbContext>((sp, opts) =>
{
    opts.UseNpgsql(connectionString);
    opts.AddInterceptors(sp.GetRequiredService<TenantRlsConnectionInterceptor>());
});

slugs, and short numeric ids while rejecting any value that could escape
the single-quoted literal.

EF Core transaction so PostgreSQL Row-Level Security policies can use

Remarks

Hooks TransactionStartedAsync / TransactionStarted rather than
ConnectionOpenedAsync: PgBouncer in transaction-pooling mode recycles the backend
connection at transaction boundaries, so setting a GUC outside an explicit transaction
would leak across tenants. Scoping to SET LOCAL (equivalently
set_config(..., is_local=true)) ties the setting to the current transaction.

Uses set_config(...) instead of SET LOCAL app.current_tenant_id = '...' because
Postgres's SET utility statement does not accept parameter binding; the function form
does, keeping the tenant id out of the SQL text (defence against log leakage / injection).

No-op when ITenantContext.TenantId is null or empty
(background jobs / setup scripts). RLS policies must be written to accept
current_setting('app.current_tenant_id', true) IS NULL as the unscoped path if those
flows need to read cross-tenant data; otherwise they must set the GUC manually.

AddKunMultiTenancy<TContext>(IServiceCollection, Action<KunMultiTenancyOptions>)

Registers the multi-tenancy services for a specific DbContext type. Must be called
BEFORE the matching AddDbContext<TContext>, and the consumer is
responsible for registering their own ITenantDbContextFactory<TContext>
when KunMultiTenancyOptions.Strategy is
TenantIsolationStrategy.SchemaPerTenant.

public static IServiceCollection AddKunMultiTenancy<TContext>(this IServiceCollection services, Action<KunMultiTenancyOptions> configure) where TContext : DbContext

Parameters

services IServiceCollection

configure Action<KunMultiTenancyOptions>

Returns

IServiceCollection

Type Parameters

TContext

Remarks

Shared: delegates to AddKunTenantRls() — no additional services
beyond the RLS interceptor and NullTenantProvisioner default.

SchemaPerTenant: registers TenantAwareModelCacheKeyFactory,
the TenantRlsTransactionInterceptor (defence-in-depth), a
Singleton SchemaPerTenantProvisioner<TContext> as the
ITenantProvisioner implementation, and binds
KunMultiTenancyOptions. Consumers must also add the schema selection
and the model-cache factory to their DbContext options, e.g.:

services.AddDbContext<CatalogDbContext>((sp, opts) =>
    opts.UseNpgsql(cs)
        .UseKunSchema(sp.GetRequiredService<ITenantContext>().TenantId ?? "public")
        .ReplaceService<IModelCacheKeyFactory, TenantAwareModelCacheKeyFactory>()
        .AddInterceptors(sp.GetRequiredService<TenantRlsTransactionInterceptor>()));

DatabasePerTenant: registers a default
OptionsBasedTenantConnectionResolver reading from
TenantsConnectionOptions plus a Singleton
DatabasePerTenantProvisioner<TContext>. Consumers are still responsible
for registering their own ITenantDbContextFactory<TContext> that
resolves the tenant's connection string via IDbConnectionResolver and
constructs a DbContext bound to that connection.

Strategy snapshotting: the KunMultiTenancyOptions.Strategy
value set by configure is captured at registration time to decide
which services to register. A subsequent
services.Configure<KunMultiTenancyOptions> that mutates
KunMultiTenancyOptions.Strategy will NOT retro-actively change the DI
wiring — the options-read path would disagree with the registered graph. Set the
strategy exactly once, inside this call's configure delegate.

before entity configurations run — tables, Outbox, and Saga storage all land under this

Remarks

Registered as a DI singleton by AddKunGateway. The cache is shared between
the public MapKunJwks route and the gated MapKunInternalJwks route
so both serve the same byte-identical document and both pay the key-rebuild
cost at most once per key-rotation event.

Thread-safe via a single lock around the cached tuple. The lock scope is tiny
(read the mtime, compare, maybe rebuild) and the rebuild path only fires when
an operator rotates the key — expected to be infrequent relative to request
volume, so lock contention is a non-issue in practice.

Remarks

The public endpoint (see JwksEndpoint.MapKunJwks) is required for any consumer — inside
or outside the cluster — to validate S2S tokens, and stays unconditionally enabled. The internal
endpoint at /internal/.well-known/jwks.json is an opt-in convenience for downstream
services that talk to the gateway through a NetworkPolicy-isolated interface and want a stable
well-known path that does NOT share lifecycle with the public route (e.g. for separate
rate-limiting or egress controls).

Gating policy: the internal route is reachable only when either (a) the host runs in the
Development environment, or (b) KunGatewayOptions.ExposeInternalJwks is
explicitly set to true. Any other environment returns 404, so forgetting to
set the flag in production fails closed.

Remarks

The implementation executes a two-command pipeline (INCR + TTL read) to obtain both
the post-increment count and the remaining TTL in one round-trip. On the first hit
(INCR returns 1), it follows up with EXPIRE to set the window TTL; subsequent hits
in the same window leave the TTL untouched.

Not a full RateLimiter subclass — this is
the low-level primitive. Full PartitionedRateLimiter<HttpContext>
integration with ASP.NET's rate-limit middleware is tracked as future work.

public interface IAuthenticatedUser : ICurrentUser

Implements

ICurrentUser

Remarks

Services that resolve the user from an S2S JWT should keep
injecting ICurrentUser. Endpoints that serve the
browser (cookie + OIDC code flow) can inject
IAuthenticatedUser to reach the cookie-only fields
without casting.

The DI registration provided by Kun.Identity.AspNetCore
binds both interfaces to the same request-scoped instance, so the
choice of injected interface is purely about the fields the caller
needs.

See docs/architecture/when-to-use-currentuser.md for the
full decision table across consumer scenarios and the anti-patterns
that should never show up in a PR (no ICurrentUserEx, no
per-service subinterface, no ClaimsPrincipal
injection as a first-class service).

KunCookieAuthApplicationBuilderExtensions

IApplicationBuilder extensions for the Kun cookie middleware.

KunCookieAuthMiddleware

Middleware that hydrates HttpContext.User from a
ISessionStore entry keyed by the session cookie.
Requests without a valid session flow through anonymously; the
middleware never writes a 401 itself — downstream authorization
policies are responsible for that.

KunCurrentUser

Request-scoped IAuthenticatedUser (and
ICurrentUser) resolver. Reads claims off
HttpContext.User — which UseKunCookieAuth populates
from ISessionStore earlier in the pipeline. Anonymous when
no IHttpContextAccessor is available or the
authentication middleware has not run.

KunIdentityAspNetCoreServiceCollectionExtensions

Registers the browser identity helpers without replacing the host's authentication scheme.

OidcLoginService

Completes the protected browser transaction before creating a local session.

OidcLogoutEndpoint

Back-channel logout mapping; authentication comes from the signed provider token, not a browser cookie.

OidcLogoutService

Validates provider logout instructions before atomically revoking local sessions.

SignInHelper

Turns a successful OIDC code-exchange into a signed-in browser
session: writes the SessionData into the configured
ISessionStore and emits the opaque session cookie on
the current response.

Classes

KunCookieAuthOptions

Options for the cookie session layer wired by
AddKunIdentity(id => id.AddCookieSession(...)). The defaults
encode the zero-trust baseline Kun.Gateway already applies to
outbound cookies.

KunCookieSessionBuilder

Configuration surface exposed by
KunIdentityBuilder.AddCookieSession(opts => ...). Inherits
every KunCookieAuthOptions field (so callers write
opts.CookieName = "kun.sid"; opts.SessionTtl = ...; as
expected) and adds the backend-selection methods
KunCookieSessionBuilder.UseInMemoryStore and KunCookieSessionBuilder.UseRedisStore.
Exactly one backend call should be made — multiple calls take
last-wins semantics because each call replaces the
ISessionStore registration on the underlying service
collection.

KunIdentityBuilder

Fluent builder surfaced by AddKunIdentity.

KunJwtBearerOptions

Validation parameters for external Bearer JWTs issued by an OIDC
provider (Authentik, Keycloak, Auth0, Azure AD, …). Feeds
KunJwtValidator.

KunJwtIssuerOptions

Signing / claims configuration for KunJwtIssuer.

KunOidcClientOptions

Per-provider configuration for KunOidcClient.

Secure-policy for KunCookieAuthOptions.Secure. Mirrors
ASP.NET Core's CookieSecurePolicy shape without taking a
dependency on that package from the core abstractions.

Mirrors ASP.NET Core's SameSiteMode shape without taking a

Remarks

This options type lives in Kun.Identity (not
Kun.Identity.AspNetCore) so non-ASP.NET-Core hosts — worker
services that replay a signed-in request, integration tests that
synthesize a session — can configure it without pulling the ASP.NET
Core dependency. KunCookieAuthOptions.SameSite and KunCookieAuthOptions.Secure
use Kun-owned enums (KunSameSiteMode,
KunCookieSecurePolicy); the middleware in
Kun.Identity.AspNetCore maps them to the equivalent ASP.NET
Core values at registration time.

CookieName

Session cookie name. Default kun.sid.

public string CookieName { get; set; }

Property Value

string

Domain

Cookie Domain. Leave null to scope the
cookie to the exact host that set it (recommended for
multi-tenant isolation; only override when the session must be
shared across subdomains).

Emit the cookie with HttpOnly. Default true
and strongly recommended to stay that way — JavaScript must not

SameSite

Secure

Absolute session lifetime. Default 8 hours. The cookie
Max-Age and the ISessionStore
entry TTL are both bound to this value at sign-in.

Property Value

TimeSpan

SlidingExpiration

When true, authenticated requests extend the
session on both the cookie and the store (matching the
SessionTtl window from the current instant). Default
true.

KunMediator

Reflection-free CQRS dispatcher. Handler lookup is O(1) via a pre-built
FrozenDictionary. All handler types are explicitly
registered at startup through KunMediatorBuilder, so no runtime
scanning or generic type construction is needed — this class is fully AOT-safe.

KunMediatorBuilder

Fluent builder used to register request handlers, pipeline behaviors, and notification
handlers with KunMediator. All registrations are performed via
compile-time-closed generics — no runtime reflection or MakeGenericType occurs.

custom resolver (subdomain-based, query-string-based, etc.) by

Marker interface for DbContexts that want the
KunMultiTenantModelCacheKeyFactory to partition EF
Core's compiled-model cache per tenant. Implementers expose the
ambient tenant id so the factory can emit a distinct cache key for
each tenant, preventing EF from folding the query-filter constant
across tenants on the first model build.

Kun.EntityFrameworkCore.KunDbContext already exposes an
equivalent TenantIdForModelCacheKey property; custom
contexts that inherit from plain DbContext
should implement this interface to opt into per-tenant isolation.

Remarks

Register on the DbContextOptionsBuilder:
.ReplaceService<IModelCacheKeyFactory, KunMultiTenantModelCacheKeyFactory>().

Without this factory, EF Core keys compiled models only on
DbContext type. The first tenant's query filter is
then baked into the shared model — subsequent tenants would read
against the first tenant's filter constant, silently leaking data
across tenant boundaries.

Interfaces

ISaga<TContext>

Defines an orchestrated saga — an ordered sequence of compensatable ISagaStep<TContext>s.
The orchestrator executes steps in forward order and compensates in reverse order on failure.

ISagaContext

Marker interface for saga context objects. Every saga context carries a unique
ISagaContext.SagaId and an optional ISagaContext.TenantId for multi-tenant scenarios.
Implementations should be serializable to JSON (used for durable state storage).

ISagaOrchestrator

Starts new saga instances and persists the initial state atomically within the caller's
ambient unit-of-work transaction. The background SagaStepExecutor then drives
step execution and compensation asynchronously.

ISagaStep<TContext>

A single compensatable step in a saga. Each step must implement both a forward
ISagaStep<TContext>.ExecuteAsync and a reverse
ISagaStep<TContext>.CompensateAsync path, both of which must be idempotent.

content:
本页由 DocFX 从 nuget.org 上 Kun.Security 2026.10.25 的 XML 注释生成，源码在 kun 仓库 src/Kun.Security（v2026.10.25）。Kun 文档与代码不一致处以代码为准（ADR-001 D1.8）；Qian 对 Kun 的选用与约束见与 Qian 的关系。

Classes

JwksEndpointExtensions

Extension methods for registering the S2S JWKS endpoint middleware.

JwksEndpointMiddleware

ASP.NET Core middleware that serves the JWKS at /.well-known/jwks.json.
Includes both the current and previous signing keys (for graceful rotation).

KunSecurityS2SJwtServiceCollectionExtensions

Extension methods for registering Kun S2S JWT issuer and verifier services.

S2SJwtIssueRequest

Input for IS2SJwtIssuer.IssueAsync.
Carries the full SAD v3.0 §12 legacy S2S claim set.

S2SJwtIssuer

ES256 implementation of IS2SJwtIssuer. Emits the SAD v3.0 §12 claim
set (sub, tenant_id, roles, optional membership_id,
optional project_id, optional trace_id) and retains the pre-existing
scope / session_id claims for OAuth2-style callers.

S2SJwtOptions

Configuration for S2S JWT issuance and verification using ES256 (ECDSA P-256).
Per the zero-trust policy, ES256 is the required algorithm for legacy S2S tokens.

S2SJwtVerifier

Verifies S2S JWT tokens using ES256 and the configured signing keys.
Supports key rotation by accepting both current and previous signing keys.

Interfaces

IS2SJwtIssuer

Issues S2S JWT tokens signed with ES256 for internal service-to-service authentication.

IS2SJwtVerifier

Verifies S2S JWT tokens issued by the gateway.

Remarks

Implementations must enforce ContentDispositionPolicy on uploads
and presigned download URLs, so that browsers never render user-uploaded
active-web types (HTML, SVG, XML, JavaScript, WASM) inline.

Classes

ContentDispositionPolicy

Policy for deciding when browsers must be forced to download (rather than render)
a stored object. Active-web MIME types (HTML/SVG/XML/JS/WASM) are served back as
attachment so that user-uploaded content cannot execute in the origin of
the download domain.

ObjectDownload

Content stream plus metadata returned from
IFileStorage.GetObjectAsync.

ObjectMetadata

Metadata describing a stored object.

ObjectSummary

IFileStorage.ListObjectsAsync.

PutObjectOptions

Options supplied when uploading an object.

StorageOptions

Configuration options for Kun.Storage.

Interfaces

IFileStorage

Abstraction for object-storage operations. Supports multiple backends
(local filesystem, S3, MinIO) behind a uniform contract.

GetPresignedPostUploadAsync(string, UploadConstraints?, TimeSpan?, CancellationToken)

Creates a presigned POST upload descriptor. The signed policy embeds
UploadConstraints.MaxBytes when set, so the backing store (not the
framework) rejects oversized uploads before any bytes are persisted. Allowed
content types are encoded into the policy when
UploadConstraints.AllowedContentTypes is supplied.

public Task<PresignedPostUpload> GetPresignedPostUploadAsync(string objectKey, UploadConstraints? constraints = null, TimeSpan? expiresIn = null, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)

Parameters

objectKey string

Target object key.

constraints UploadConstraints?

Optional upload constraints. When null, no size/type
limits are baked into the policy.

expiresIn TimeSpan?

Lifetime of the signed policy.

cancellationToken CancellationToken

Cancellation token.

Returns

Task<PresignedPostUpload>

Remarks

Not supported on the local-filesystem implementation: signing a POST policy is an
S3-specific construct with no meaningful analogue for a developer-local store.
Callers that need dev-time presigned uploads should use
LocalFileSystemStorage.GetPresignedUploadAsync;
callers that need MaxBytes-in-signature enforcement must swap to Kun.Storage.S3
against an S3-compatible endpoint (e.g. MinIO for dev).

GetPresignedUploadAsync(string, string, UploadConstraints?, TimeSpan?, CancellationToken)

record carries the exact HTTP headers the caller must send so server-side

public Task<PresignedUploadUrl> GetPresignedUploadAsync(string objectKey, string contentType, UploadConstraints? constraints = null, TimeSpan? expiresIn = null, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)

constraints UploadConstraints?

expiresIn TimeSpan?

cancellationToken CancellationToken

Task<PresignedUploadUrl>

Remarks

The PUT URL returned here cannot embed UploadConstraints.MaxBytes in
the signature; consumers that need size enforcement at the S3 layer should use
IFileStorage.GetPresignedPostUploadAsync instead — its signed POST policy bakes
content-length-range into the signature so S3 rejects oversized bodies with
HTTP 400 before any bytes are persisted.

Alibaba Cloud OSS implementation of IFileStorage using the native
Aliyun.OSS.SDK.NetCore client.

public sealed class OssFileStorage : IFileStorage

Inheritance

Remarks

Why native and not the S3-compatible path: OSS exposes an S3-compatible surface, but
its presigned URLs are validated with OSS's own signature algorithm — not AWS SigV4. An AWS
SDK client pointed at an OSS endpoint emits SigV4-signed URLs that OSS rejects, so presigned
upload/download (the core of this contract) does not work over Kun.Storage.S3. This
type therefore wraps the native SDK and is the supported way to target OSS.

Security guarantee (M1): OssFileStorage.GetPresignedDownloadAsync ALWAYS sets
response-content-disposition=attachment on the signed URL when the stored object's
content type is one of ActiveWebContentTypes.Value, regardless of
DownloadOptions.ForceDownload.

Async posture: the Aliyun SDK exposes only synchronous and APM (Begin/End) operations,
no TAP. Network calls are offloaded with Run
so callers keep an async surface; the token cancels queueing, not an in-flight OSS request.
Presigned-URL generation is pure local signing (no I/O) and completes synchronously.

Content-Disposition: attachment on presigned download URLs whose
ObjectMetadata.ContentType is contained in this set, regardless
of whether the caller requested DownloadOptions.ForceDownload.

Namespace: Kun.Storage
Assembly: Kun.Storage.Abstractions.dll

Transport-agnostic object-storage abstraction used by Kun services to upload,
download, and manage blob artifacts (attachments, user uploads, exported files).
Implementations map the seven operations to a backing store (local filesystem,
Amazon S3, MinIO, Azure Blob, GCS).

public interface IFileStorage

Remarks

Object keys are relative, forward-slash-delimited paths (e.g. tenants/42/avatar.png).
They do not include a leading slash and do not identify the bucket / root — the
implementation resolves those from its configured options.

Implementations MUST force Content-Disposition: attachment on presigned
download URLs whose stored content type is in
ActiveWebContentTypes.Value, even if
DownloadOptions.ForceDownload is false. This defends against
cross-origin script execution when a tenant-uploaded HTML/SVG/XML blob is opened
inline by a browser.

Creates a presigned POST upload descriptor. The signed policy embeds
UploadConstraints.MaxBytes when set, so the backing store (not the
framework) rejects oversized uploads before any bytes are persisted. Allowed
content types are encoded into the policy when

record carries the exact HTTP headers the caller must send so server-side
constraint enforcement works.

The PUT URL returned here cannot embed UploadConstraints.MaxBytes in
the signature; consumers that need size enforcement at the S3 layer should use
IFileStorage.GetPresignedPostUploadAsync instead — its signed POST policy bakes
content-length-range into the signature so S3 rejects oversized bodies with
HTTP 400 before any bytes are persisted.

OutboxAssertions

Fluent assertion extensions for EF-persisted OutboxMessage
state. Helpers come in two overload families:
one on IEnumerable of OutboxMessage for

and the distinct event-type IDs actually present (so the failure
message tells the consumer what WAS staged, not just what wasn't).

Classes

ValidationPipelineBehavior<TRequest, TResponse>

Pipeline behavior that runs every registered IValidator<T> against the
incoming request and throws ValidationException if any report errors.

For Result-based semantics (returning Result.Fail(Error.Validation(...)) instead
of throwing), compose this behavior inside a user-written "ValidationResultAdapter"
behavior — shipped as a follow-up.

ValidationResultPipelineBehavior<TRequest, TValue>

Pipeline behavior that runs every registered IValidator<T>
against the incoming request and returns
Result<TValue>.Fail(Error.Validation("request.invalid", …))
instead of throwing when any report errors. Companion to the
exception-throwing ValidationPipelineBehavior<TRequest, TResponse>
for handlers that deliberately compose via Result<T>
and want validation failures to surface through the normal
railway pipeline (see docs/architecture/ADR-011-Result-async-extensions.md
and docs/architecture/ADR-014-Validation-Result-behavior.md).

ValidationResultPipelineBehavior<TRequest>

Non-generic variant of
ValidationResultPipelineBehavior<TRequest, TValue> for
handlers whose response is the non-generic Result
(void commands with no return value). Returns
Result.Fail(Error.Validation("request.invalid", …))
instead of throwing when validators report errors. Closes ADR-014
§F1 follow-up.

title: 能力与函数
content:
能力目录

组件把自己的能力登记进能力目录（qian.capabilities），分四类：命令、查询、事件、实体。

组件在 Apply 中用 ctx.ProvideCapability<TRequest, TResponse>() 登记能力，绑定携带源生成的契约，请求与响应的 JSON Schema 由类型信息派生；目录只列这些绑定里、当前 scope 已挂载且 Ready 的能力。

platform profile 宿主必须调用 services.AddQianCapabilities()，登记时就生成目录条目并预编译输入校验器（漏掉时退化为首次读目录或调用时才编译）。不合格的契约（输入含 tenantId 等租户字段、Schema 无法可靠校验）抛 CapabilityContractException，带组件 ID、能力短名与 JSON Pointer（如 qian.sample.crm/customer.export#/inputSchema/properties/tenantId），组件挂载失败；问题在登记时暴露，不会留到第一次调用。

GET /api/capabilities?kind=command|query|event|entity&q= 按调用者权限与当前 scope 的 restrict 过滤，被过滤的项不出现；响应信封 { items, ttlMs, cacheScope: "private" } 的冻结 Schema 是 contracts/v0/capability-catalog.schema.json。

POST /api/capabilities/{plugin}/{name}/invoke 是通用执行入口，规则见下节。

GET /api/capabilities/openapi.json 聚合全部已挂载组件的 OpenAPI 3.1（需认证，不等于公开 OpenAPI）；写类能力的路径列出 Idempotency-Key 参数、Idempotent-Replayed 响应头与两种 409（CONFLICT、CAPABILITY_REPLAY_UNAVAILABLE）。

Agent 用的工具定义由能力目录机械生成，保证 schema 不漂移；暴露哪些、怎么描述，经 agent.expose 单独策划（ADR-016 D16.10）。

代码与唯一清单

每个 [QianPlugin] 组件对应一份 .qian-plugin/plugin.json 和一个入口。同一程序集可包含多个不同组件 ID；qian-plugin check|sync 按目标清单 ID 选择，不合并不同组件的依赖。多组件程序集的 [Capability] 必须填写 ComponentId。契约包装器、动态表面适配器及宿主子插件通过仓库分类门记录归属，不各造一份清单。

已派生	代码来源与落点
服务与具名贡献	Inject / Provide、CommandPolicies 与按真实注册表符号绑定的 Contributes → inject / provides
形态与入口	QianPlugin → runtime.form / runtime.entry
工具	Capability 与源生成 JsonTypeInfo，或与实际绑定共用的静态 CapabilitySource → tools/*.json
配置契约	QianConfigSchema 的完整代码声明 → runtime.configSchema 与对应 Schema 文件
权限与事件	Permission / QianEvent → metadata/permissions.json、metadata/events.json；带清单侧的来源与派生指针，不放进 plugin.json

id、版本、展示、策略、scope、包/镜像信息及表面路径仍手写；没有代码声明的权限文件与角色模板继续手写。动态 Inject、动态贡献名和未知上下文逃逸会报编译诊断，不生成空结果。需要不同构造模式的实现由固定薄入口明确依赖、委托目标与服务输出，真实装载负责验证提供项。

同程序集的多个 Provider 使用同一事件 Definition 时，由一个组件通过 MetadataTypes 拥有声明，其它组件以 SharedEvents 显式引用；生成的事件记录带 definitionComponent，保持名称、模式、载荷类型与来源同源。此机制只共享事件契约，不能共享权限，也不放宽未知上下文逃逸的诊断。

sync 沿既有表面目录写入，check 只读并报告文件与 JSON Pointer。清单保存权限、事件与配置文件的所属组件和内容哈希；手改这些文件后保留并报冲突，工具文件通过所属标记区分手写与派生。无组件注解、ID 不匹配、第二清单、手写覆盖、路径越界都有各自的 SDK 错误码及 errors[]。CI 自动发现所有代码入口并检查清单，同时拒绝漏分类的新实现。

R94 将 IQianPlugin 基类、客户端门面、生命周期钩子基类与 DI 注册代码生成推迟到 S2；S1 继续使用接口和 ctx.Inject。[QianJob] 属于 S1-SCH-001 的调度器交付，不在本次生成器补齐范围内。UI/低代码及 Wasm 表面按各自 S2 规划，代码热装卸尚未承诺。清单已经派生不代表真实安装验收完成，x-skeleton 仍按每个组件的安装门维护。

通用执行入口

POST /api/capabilities/{plugin}/{name}/invoke 先重做与目录相同的过滤（不可见与不存在一样 404），再按条目 inputSchema 校验请求体（不符返回 400 INPUT_INVALID，errors[] 带 JSON Pointer；请求体读不成确定的 JSON 值，如成员重名或有绝对值超过 decimal 范围约 7.9e28 的数，返回 400 BAD_REQUEST），然后走组件自己的命令管道，租户、授权与审计照常生效。

写类能力可以带幂等键，只读能力（sideEffect: read）忽略它、每次都执行：

头	方向	含义
Idempotency-Key	请求	UUID 文本，可带引号；多值、空值、全零或非 UUID 返回 400 BAD_REQUEST
Idempotent-Replayed: true	响应	这次是回放：响应体与首次成功响应逐字节相同，没有再执行

同一租户、同一主体、同一能力、同一键在 24 小时内的重复请求都不会再执行。409 分两种：

CONFLICT：同键而输入不同，或同键请求仍在执行。改用新的键，或等前一个请求结束再重试。

CAPABILITY_REPLAY_UNAVAILABLE：同键请求已经执行成功，但回执没有保存响应体，无法回放。只有 dataClassification 为 public 或 internal 的能力保存响应体：pii、finance、secret 不保存，未知分级也不保存；响应超过组件配置 receiptMaxBytes（默认 64 KiB）时同样不保存。应通过查询确认结果，不要换新键重试，换键会再执行一次。

[Capability] 的 DataClassification 默认 internal，也就是默认把响应体明文存进回执表，24 小时内同键请求原样回放。响应含个人信息、财务或机密数据的能力要显式标注，如 DataClassification = "pii"（finance、secret 同理）；参考应用响应含客户名称的 customer.* 能力都标为 pii。

执行失败不留回执，同一个键可以带正确的输入重试。服务端在执行后、写回执前崩溃时，5 分钟租约到期后的重试会再执行一次，所以写类能力仍要在 inputSchema 里带业务幂等键（idempotencyKey）。

函数

function 表面（Wasm 沙箱内运行的函数）是 S2 可选能力；Agent 生成的代码只落在 function 沙箱里（ADR-016 D16.11）。

详见 PRD §7.2。

title: ADR-001: Do Not Introduce a New Kun.Identity Module
content:
本页镜像自 kun 仓库 docs/architecture/ADR-001-Kun.Identity-module-decision.md（v2026.10.25）。Kun 文档与代码不一致处以代码为准（ADR-001 D1.8）；Qian 对 Kun 的选用与约束见与 Qian 的关系。改动请提到 kun 仓库。

Status: Accepted
Date: 2026-04-22
Author: claude-official (Planner)
Context: Phase 1 gap audit (kun/docs/neuroagent-phase1-gap.md) flagged P1-KN-002 / P1-KN-003 as "already present"; a prior planning round (ralplan v1) incorrectly invented P1-KN-004 / P1-KN-005 as new Kun.Identity work. This ADR records the explicit decision not to create a dedicated Kun.Identity module and instead consume existing capabilities.

Decision

No new Kun.Identity module will be created.

Authentication and identity concerns for NeuroAgent Phase 1 will be handled by:

Kun.Gateway — OIDC IdP (Authentik) token exchange → internal S2S JWT

Kun.Security — S2S JWT validation, JWKS endpoint consumption, claim extraction

NeuroAgent-csharp Edge service — direct AddJwtBearer wiring against Kun.Security primitives

Decision Drivers

Capability already exists — Kun.Gateway (OIDC→S2S conversion) and Kun.Security (S2S validation + JWKS) together cover the full identity lifecycle needed for Phase 1.

No gap in Phase 1 — The gap audit (neuroagent-phase1-gap.md §4-5) identified P1-KN-001 (Kun.Storage) as the only missing Kun module for Phase 1. Identity needs are satisfied by existing modules.

Avoid framework bloat — A new module would add maintenance surface (release, versioning, AOT verification, documentation) without adding net-new capability.

Downstream simplicity — Edge service consuming AddJwtBearer + Kun.Security is less indirection than routing through an additional framework module.

Alternatives Considered

Alternative	Description	Why Rejected
A. Create Kun.Identity	New module with IIdentityService, IUserContext, IPermissionChecker abstractions	Duplicates Kun.Security (S2S validation) and Kun.Gateway (OIDC exchange). Would require neuroagent-csharp to learn another framework module for no new capability.
B. Extract identity types into Kun.Identity	Move IUserContext, claim constants, etc. from Kun.Security into a slimmer Kun.Identity	Refactoring churn with zero functional gain. Would break existing consumers of Kun.Security.
C. Keep as-is (status quo)	No new module; consume existing Kun.Gateway + Kun.Security	Selected. Satisfies all Phase 1 requirements with zero new code.

Why Chosen

Status quo (Alternative C) is the only option that satisfies all drivers without trade-offs:

Zero new framework code to maintain

Zero migration for existing consumers

Aligns with gap audit finding that Phase 1's only real Kun blocker is P1-KN-001 (Storage)

Consequences

Positive

No framework release cycle consumed by a new module

No AOT verification work for a new assembly

No documentation / sample / AGENTS.md debt for Kun.Identity

Negative / Trade-offs

NeuroAgent-csharp Edge must own the AddJwtBearer wiring — this is consumer-specific config (Authentik issuer URL, client ID, etc.) and does not belong in Kun anyway. The wiring lives in neuroagent-csharp where it is editable by the consumer team.

If future phases need cross-cutting identity abstractions (e.g., IPermissionChecker with policy store), we will revisit this ADR. At that point the scope will be broader than Phase 1 and a new module may be justified.

Risks

Risk	Mitigation
Future identity needs outgrow Kun.Security + Kun.Gateway	ADR is revisable; gate is "cross-cutting abstraction needed by 2+ consumers"
Edge service OIDC wiring diverges from Kun patterns	Review Edge service PRs for Kun.Security consumption; do not allow custom JWT validation logic

Follow-ups

P1-CS-007 (Edge OIDC wiring) — implement in neuroagent-csharp using AddJwtBearer + Kun.Security primitives. No Kun work required.

P1-CS-010 (Gateway YARP + OIDC exchange) — Kun.Gateway already owns this pattern; verify it is wired correctly in the Gateway service.

Retrospective note — The v1 planner mistake (inventing P1-KN-004/005 without reading gap audit) is recorded in project memory as a discipline reminder: read authoritative specs before dispatching framework tasks.

title: ADR-003: Introduce Kun.Audit and Kun.Audit.EntityFrameworkCore Modules
content:
本页镜像自 kun 仓库 docs/architecture/ADR-003-Kun.Audit-module.md（v2026.10.25）。Kun 文档与代码不一致处以代码为准（ADR-001 D1.8）；Qian 对 Kun 的选用与约束见与 Qian 的关系。改动请提到 kun 仓库。

Status: Accepted
Date: 2026-04-22
Author: claude-kun (Kun framework specialist)
Context: neuroagent-phase1-gap.md §2 flagged audit logging as missing for P1-CS-019. An initial attempt by the business-services pane (glm) to build the feature inside neuroagent-csharp stalled at the framework boundary: per the 路由边界铁律 in the project CLAUDE.md, cross-cutting capabilities that could be reused by other services must land in kun/, not as a private fork inside a consumer repository. Handoff P1-KN-Audit-handoff.md captured the expected deliverables.

Decision

Introduce two new framework modules:

Module	Layer	IsAotCandidate	Responsibility
Kun.Audit	Abstraction	true	IAuditWriter / IAuditReader / AuditableAttribute, AuditLog POCO, NullAuditWriter, EventBusAuditWriter, AddKunAudit DI
Kun.Audit.EntityFrameworkCore	Infrastructure	false	AuditSaveChangesInterceptor, AuditLogConfiguration, EfAuditWriter<TDbContext>, UseEntityFramework<TDbContext>() DI

The original handoff brief (P1-KN-Audit-handoff.md) specified a single
Kun.Audit module with IsAotCandidate=true. That specification is
incompatible with the four-layer / AOT rules recorded in
CLAUDE.md §Architectural constraints — EF Core 10 is not yet fully AOT
compatible, which is why Kun.EntityFrameworkCore itself ships with
IsAotCandidate=false. Bundling EF Core types into an AOT-candidate
module would fail dotnet publish -p:PublishAot=true /warnaserror at
CI. Per the "Stop gate" rule on AOT warnings, this ADR records the
split decision instead of silently flipping IsAotCandidate=false on
the single-module variant.

Decision Drivers

Layering rule — Abstractions must not depend on EF Core. Putting the
interceptor (an EF Core type) in the same csproj as the
IAuditWriter contract would elevate EF Core into the Abstraction
layer and cascade a transitive EF Core dependency onto every
consumer of Kun.Audit.

AOT strategy — Kun.Mediator, Kun.Core, Kun.EventBus etc. are
AOT-strict and CI enforces zero AOT warnings. EF Core 10's incomplete
AOT support means any module that references EF Core types cannot be
AOT-strict. Split preserves the option for full-AOT consumers to use
EventBusAuditWriter (abstraction-only, AOT-safe) while still offering
EfAuditWriter<TDbContext> to trim-safe deployments.

Composability — Consumers pick exactly one writer via the
KunAuditBuilder fluent chain: UseEventBus() or
UseEntityFramework<TDbContext>(). Additional writers (SIEM forwarder,
hash-chain tamper-evidence, file append-log) can be added as further
UseX() extensions on KunAuditBuilder without touching core.

Zero-config safe default — A NullAuditWriter is registered by
default so that a consumer who only calls AddKunAudit() (without
picking a backend) doesn't crash at first use. It logs a single
warning so operators notice the misconfiguration without log-flood.

Alternatives Considered

Alternative	Description	Why Rejected
A. Single Kun.Audit module with EF Core inside	Matches handoff text literally; minimises module count	Violates layering + AOT rules. AOT publish would fail at CI; consumer of IAuditWriter abstraction would transitively pull EF Core.
B. Single Kun.Audit with IsAotCandidate=false	Keeps module count low; drops AOT promise for audit users	Eliminates the AOT-friendly fan-out path (EventBusAuditWriter) — consumers running full AOT would have no audit option at all.
C. Fold into Kun.EntityFrameworkCore	Reuse the existing infrastructure module; no new csproj	Audit is a distinct concern with its own versioning cadence, own pipeline behavior surface, and its own consumer (compliance team). Bloating Kun.EntityFrameworkCore makes the dependency graph coarser than necessary.
D. Split into Abstraction + Infrastructure (selected)	Two new csproj entries; mirrors Kun.EventBus + Kun.EventBus.RabbitMQ pattern that is already established	Slight module-count overhead, offset by preserving layering & AOT promises and giving consumers a clean pick-one-writer API.

Why Chosen

Option D is the only alternative that respects both the layering
four-layer flow and the AOT-candidate invariant. It also matches the
existing Kun.EventBus → Kun.EventBus.RabbitMQ pattern, so there is
no new architectural convention to learn.

Integration Points

┌──────────────────────────┐
│  Consumer business code  │                 emits IAggregateRoot / IMultiTenant
└──────────────────────────┘
           │
           ▼
┌──────────────────────────┐
│  AppDbContext (consumer) │         ← AddInterceptors(AuditSaveChangesInterceptor)
└──────────────────────────┘
           │ SaveChangesAsync
           ▼
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  AuditSaveChangesInterceptor                 │  (Kun.Audit.EntityFrameworkCore)
│    SavingChangesAsync:  walk ChangeTracker,  │
│                         buffer PendingAudit  │
│    SavedChangesAsync:   foreach pending →    │
│                         IAuditWriter.Write   │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────┘
           │
           ▼
┌──────────────────────────┐
│  IAuditWriter            │   (Kun.Audit abstraction)
└──────────────────────────┘
   │                    │                    │
   │ EfAuditWriter      │ EventBusAuditWriter│ custom
   ▼                    ▼                    ▼
 DbSet<AuditLog>    Outbox → RabbitMQ     …

Actor & trace attribution is resolved from the existing Kun.Core
primitives, so no new infrastructure is added:

ITenantContext.TenantId → AuditLog.TenantId

ICurrentUser.UserId → AuditLog.ActorId

ITracedCurrentUser.TraceId / Activity.Current.TraceId → AuditLog.TraceId

ISystemClock.UtcNow → AuditLog.Timestamp

Schema & Query Indexes

The EF configuration creates four B-tree indexes to cover the known
query patterns:

Index	Pattern
(tenant_id, timestamp DESC)	"show me this tenant's recent activity"
(tenant_id, actor_id, timestamp DESC)	per-user drill-down
(tenant_id, action, timestamp DESC)	compliance queries (all user.login.*)
(tenant_id, resource_type, resource_id)	resource history

The partitioning strategy (monthly by timestamp) is deferred to the
consumer's migration — PostgreSQL declarative partitioning is not
expressible in IEntityTypeConfiguration<T> and must be emitted via
raw SQL in a migration. Consumers that expect >10M audit rows / month
should add declarative monthly partitioning; the immutability +
append-only index design is already partition-friendly.

Security / Compliance Constraints (per handoff §Security)

Constraint	How it's addressed in this PR
Tenant isolation	AuditLog implements IMultiTenant; when stored in a KunDbContext-derived context, the framework-wide automatic tenant global query filter applies.
Append-only	The interceptor only ever adds AuditLog rows; it never modifies / deletes. Consumers should revoke UPDATE / DELETE on audit_logs at the DB role level — the framework cannot enforce that from code.
PII handling	KunAuditOptions.CaptureEntityPayload = false disables payload-snapshot capture globally. Per-entity redaction is a future extension — consumers that need it should implement a custom IAuditWriter decorator.
Retention	Kun does not own retention; consumers schedule a purge job against audit_logs WHERE timestamp < now() - interval 'X days' using an admin role that has DELETE privileges the application role does not.
Tamper-evidence (hash chain)	Deferred. Requires either a trigger or a dedicated writer that reads the prior row's content_hash. Captured as follow-up, tracked separately.

AOT Considerations

Kun.Audit passes dotnet publish -p:PublishAot=true /warnaserror —
it has been added to the AOT publish matrix in
.github/workflows/ci.yml.

Kun.Audit.EntityFrameworkCore is trim-safe only. Adding it to
the CI AOT matrix would regress the build because EF Core 10 itself
is not AOT-strict.

The interceptor builds its JSON payload via Utf8JsonWriter (no
runtime reflection) so the type can be hoisted to an AOT-strict
module in a future release if EF Core's AOT support matures. No
code is reached that calls JsonSerializer.Serialize(object) or
Activator.CreateInstance.

Consequences

Positive

Clear layering — consumers pick abstraction vs. infrastructure as
they do for Kun.EventBus / Kun.EventBus.RabbitMQ.

Full-AOT consumers retain an audit option (EventBusAuditWriter).

Unblocks P1-CS-019 / 020 / 021 / 022 without forking audit logic in
neuroagent-csharp.

Negative / Trade-offs

Two new csproj entries instead of one — marginal cost, but real.

Consumers wiring up audit must call three methods:
AddKunAudit().AddKunAuditEntityFrameworkCore().UseEntityFramework<T>().
A single convenience extension (AddFullAuditWithEf<T>()) could be
added later if this ergonomic proves painful.

Risks

Risk	Mitigation
Interceptor emits noisy audits for trivial writes (e.g. auto-updated UpdatedAt timestamps)	The interceptor already filters to aggregate roots; consumers can further scope by registering a custom IAuditWriter decorator that drops on PayloadJson content.
SwallowWriterExceptions=true (default) masks writer outages	Logged at Error level with correlation data; compliance-critical deployments should set SwallowWriterExceptions=false and accept that audit-infra outages block business writes.
No hash-chain today → tampering of DB rows not detectable	Documented; follow-up captured below. Immutability at the DB role layer is still the primary defense.

Follow-ups

Hash-chain tamper evidence — write a HashChainAuditWriter decorator
that maintains a prev_hash + content_hash column pair; add matching
column + migration guidance to the EF configuration.

Mediator Pipeline Behavior for AuditableAttribute — capture
Command-level audits (login, export, permission grant) that don't
trigger any change-tracker entry. Live in Kun.Audit (abstraction
side) since pipeline behaviors are Mediator-layer concerns.

Compliance query DTOs in Kun.Audit — add paginated DTOs that
consumers can project via IAuditReader for P1-CS-020 (compliance
report API).

Per-entity PII redaction via an optional IAuditPayloadRedactor
injected into the interceptor.

Declarative monthly partitioning recipe in docs/guides/ once
a consumer hits the 10M-rows-per-month threshold.

References

Handoff brief: /home/dawn/project/neuroagent/.omc/autopilot/P1-KN-Audit-handoff.md

Gap audit: docs/neuroagent-phase1-gap.md §2, §3.2, §4 "需新建"

Layering rule: CLAUDE.md §Architectural constraints (Four-layer dependency flow)

AOT rule: CLAUDE.md §Architectural constraints (AOT compatibility)

Related ADR: ADR-001-Kun.Identity-module-decision.md — the counterpart
decision not to create Identity module, based on the same audit
principles.

title: ADR-004: Introduce Kun.Observability Module
content:
本页镜像自 kun 仓库 docs/architecture/ADR-004-Kun.Observability-module.md（v2026.10.25）。Kun 文档与代码不一致处以代码为准（ADR-001 D1.8）；Qian 对 Kun 的选用与约束见与 Qian 的关系。改动请提到 kun 仓库。

Status: Accepted
Date: 2026-04-22
Author: claude-kun (Kun framework specialist)
Context: neuroagent-csharp has been maintaining a ServiceDefaults/Extensions.cs::ConfigureOpenTelemetry helper that stitches together the OpenTelemetry SDK, four instrumentation packages, and an OTLP exporter. Every new consumer repository re-copies the same boilerplate. samples/Kun.Sample.Shared/OpenTelemetryExtensions.cs carries a partial twin that lacks EF Core and runtime instrumentation. docs/observability/tracing-tour.md already references an AddKunObservability extension as if it exists — this ADR makes that reference load-bearing.

Decision

Introduce a new framework module Kun.Observability exposing a single
entry point:

services.AddKunObservability(Action<KunObservabilityOptions>? configure = null);

The module owns:

The canonical list of Kun ActivitySources
(Kun.Mediator, Kun.EventBus.Outbox, Kun.Grpc, Kun.Saga) —
kept in KunActivitySources so future sources are tracked in a
single place.

Per-instrumentation toggles (IncludeAspNetCore,
IncludeHttpClient, IncludeEfCore, IncludeRuntime) that default
to true so zero-config matches neuroagent's current shape.

Per-pillar toggles (TracingEnabled, MetricsEnabled,
LoggingEnabled) for background workers or specialized hosts that
only need a subset.

Service identity (ServiceName, ServiceVersion) projected into
the OTel resource.

Optional OtlpEndpoint override; when unset, the OTel SDK reads
OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT (which .NET Aspire sets
automatically).

An internal idempotency marker so repeated AddKunObservability
calls in the same service collection register OTel once — important
because shared libraries may call the extension defensively.

Module Shape and AOT

Property	Value
Layer	Infrastructure — carries OpenTelemetry package dependencies
<IsAotCandidate>	true — validated locally via dotnet publish -p:PublishAot=true /warnaserror up to the native-link stage (clang gap only)
Package feed	OpenTelemetry 1.11.2 + OpenTelemetry.Instrumentation.* 1.11.1 + OpenTelemetry.Instrumentation.EntityFrameworkCore 1.12.0-beta.1 + OpenTelemetry.Instrumentation.Runtime 1.11.1

The AspNetCore + HttpClient + EF Core + Runtime instrumentation
packages bundled into the module all pass the trim / AOT analyzer in
the 1.11.x line. docs/observability/tracing-tour.md §Gateway
observability gap describes a prior state where OTel instrumentation
was not AOT-safe; that note is now obsolete for AspNetCore / Http /
Runtime / EF Core (1.12.0-beta.1 onward) and Kun.Gateway can opt in
by calling AddKunObservability.

If an OTel package upgrade regresses AOT compatibility, treat it as
a stop-gate: pin the prior version or open a follow-up ADR for an
explicit IsAotCandidate=false flip. Do not silently downgrade the
module.

Alternatives Considered

Alternative	Why Rejected
A. Keep a per-consumer ConfigureOpenTelemetry helper	Drift between services. Four different service repos would maintain near-duplicate wiring. Already observed in the neuroagent-csharp vs. Kun.Sample.Shared divergence.
B. Put the wiring in Kun.AspNetCore	Kun.AspNetCore is host-layer and specific to HTTP. A background worker that wants OTel without ASP.NET Core would still pay the transitive dependency. Observability is a distinct concern.
C. Leave it in Kun.Sample.Shared	Samples are opinionated; copying an opinion into production services is a known anti-pattern. The framework needs a first-class module.
D. New Kun.Observability module (selected)	Clean separation from host layer; consumers opt in via a single Add… call; options carry the choice of pillars and instrumentation set.

Integration Points

Once AddKunObservability is wired in a host, the pipeline
automatically captures:

Mediator.Send {RequestTypeName} — via Kun.Mediator.TracingBehavior

outbox.publish — via Kun.EventBus.OutboxPublisherBackgroundService

grpc.server — via Kun.Grpc.KunTracingInterceptor

saga.step.execute / saga.step.compensate — via Kun.Saga.SagaStepExecutor

plus HTTP server, HTTP client, EF Core, and runtime metrics when the
respective toggles stay at their default of true.

W3C Trace Context propagation is the OpenTelemetry 1.x default;
AddKunObservability inherits that behaviour and does not register
any custom propagator.

Consequences

Positive

neuroagent-csharp and any future consumer repo can replace the
hand-rolled OTel helper with a single line.

Framework upgrades that add a new ActivitySource only need a patch
to KunActivitySources.All — consumers pick it up automatically.

Kun.Observability is packaged as a NuGet; versioning is visible.

Negative / Trade-offs

One additional module to build, test, and publish per release.

Transitive dependency surface grows — every host that calls
AddKunObservability now pulls in the EF Core instrumentation
package even if the host never touches EF Core. Consumers that care
can flip IncludeEfCore = false; the instrumentation code still
ships in the assembly but is not activated.

Risks

Risk	Mitigation
OTel 1.12.x upgrade breaks AOT	Stop-gate rule; CI AOT matrix includes Kun.Observability.
Double registration in consumer composition	Idempotency marker short-circuits second-call wiring; covered by AddKunObservability_IsIdempotent test.
Consumer wants a non-OTLP exporter	Options can be extended — add a ConfigureTracer / ConfigureMeter hook as a follow-up without breaking the current surface.

Follow-ups

Migrate neuroagent-csharp/ServiceDefaults to call
builder.Services.AddKunObservability(o => o.ServiceName = …)
instead of the current local helper.

Retire samples/Kun.Sample.Shared/OpenTelemetryExtensions.cs
in favor of the new module once the samples build green.

Expose a ConfigureTracer / ConfigureMeter / ConfigureLogger
extensibility hook for consumers that want to add extra
ActivitySources, metric instruments, or exporters.

Revisit Kun.Gateway observability gap noted in
tracing-tour.md §Gateway observability gap. With OTel 1.11+
AOT-clean, Gateway can opt in without losing AOT posture.

References

Handoff: task brief P1-KN-Observability

docs/observability/tracing-tour.md — span catalog the module must
keep current

neuroagent-csharp/src/NeuroAgent.ServiceDefaults/Extensions.cs —
the pattern being abstracted

samples/Kun.Sample.Shared/OpenTelemetryExtensions.cs — to be
retired

title: ADR-005: Introduce Kun.Caching Module
content:
本页镜像自 kun 仓库 docs/architecture/ADR-005-Kun.Caching-module.md（v2026.10.25）。Kun 文档与代码不一致处以代码为准（ADR-001 D1.8）；Qian 对 Kun 的选用与约束见与 Qian 的关系。改动请提到 kun 仓库。

Status: Accepted
Date: 2026-04-22
Author: claude-kun (Kun framework specialist)
Context: neuroagent-csharp has been calling services.AddStackExchangeRedisCache(...) directly from each service's Program.cs and hand-rolling IDistributedCache-based cache-aside logic (P1-CS-REDIS). Each service repeats the same serialization, key-prefixing, TTL-normalization, and single-flight boilerplate. Kun Framework has no unified cache abstraction — consumers choose between raw IMemoryCache, raw IDistributedCache, or the OSS HybridCache preview. This ADR introduces Kun.Caching to consolidate the pattern.

Decision

Introduce a new framework module Kun.Caching with a single public
contract:

public interface IKunCache
{
    Task<T?> GetAsync<T>(string key, CancellationToken ct = default);
    Task SetAsync<T>(string key, T value, TimeSpan? ttl = null, CancellationToken ct = default);
    Task RemoveAsync(string key, CancellationToken ct = default);
    Task<T> GetOrSetAsync<T>(string key, Func<CancellationToken, Task<T>> factory, TimeSpan? ttl = null, CancellationToken ct = default);
}

Two implementations ship in the module:

MemoryKunCache — wraps IMemoryCache. Stores T directly (no
serialization hop). Intended for in-process caches and tests.

RedisKunCache — wraps IDistributedCache (the
Microsoft.Extensions.Caching.StackExchangeRedis registration).
Serializes values via a pluggable IKunCacheSerializer; default is
SystemTextJsonCacheSerializer.

DI entry point is a fluent builder, mirroring the pattern established
by Kun.Audit and Kun.Storage:

services.AddKunCaching(o =>
{
    o.KeyPrefix = "platform:";
    o.DefaultTtl = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(10);
    o.FallbackToMemoryOnRedisFailure = true;
}).UseRedis(connectionString);

Module Shape and AOT

Property	Value
Layer	Infrastructure — references Microsoft.Extensions.Caching.* + StackExchange.Redis
<IsAotCandidate>	true — local dotnet publish -p:PublishAot=true /warnaserror passes the IL + trim analyzer stage with zero warnings
AOT escape hatch	IKunCache generic methods + IKunCacheSerializer are annotated with [RequiresUnreferencedCode] + [RequiresDynamicCode]. Callers either inherit the requirement through the same attributes or replace the default serializer with a source-generated JsonSerializerContext implementation

Alternatives Considered

Alternative	Why Rejected
A. Recommend Microsoft.Extensions.Caching.Hybrid	HybridCache is preview, its API is generic over HybridCacheEntryOptions, and its L2 backend is only IDistributedCache. The same boilerplate returns — consumers still build their own service wrapper.
B. Keep consumers on raw IDistributedCache	Each service re-implements serialization and single-flight. That is the status quo being replaced.
C. New Kun.Caching.Hybrid that wraps HybridCache	Possible follow-up once HybridCache GAs, but doesn't solve the API drift today.
D. New Kun.Caching module with two impls (selected)	Matches the idiomatic Kun module pattern (see Kun.EventBus vs. Kun.EventBus.RabbitMQ), handles both in-process and cross-process cases behind one surface, and lets consumers migrate from AddStackExchangeRedisCache with a single call.

Design Notes

Key prefix: KunCachingOptions.KeyPrefix is prepended to every
key before hitting the backend. Ideal for namespacing per-service
caches on a shared Redis instance (e.g. "platform:" vs "edge:").

Default TTL: when a caller omits the ttl argument,
KunCachingOptions.DefaultTtl applies. When both are null the
entry never expires — Redis default. Memory cache never-expires
entries still obey MemoryCacheOptions.SizeLimit-driven eviction
if the consumer set one.

Single-flight GetOrSetAsync: a per-key SemaphoreSlim pool
guarantees the value factory runs at most once under concurrent
access on the same process. The pool is reference-counted —
semaphores are removed when the last waiter releases, so the memory
footprint is bounded by the in-flight working set, not the lifetime
key universe. Cross-process single-flight is out of scope; callers
that need it compose a Redis distributed lock separately.

Redis fail-open: when
KunCachingOptions.FallbackToMemoryOnRedisFailure = true,
RedisKunCache catches RedisConnectionException,
RedisTimeoutException, and SocketException, logs at Warning,
and routes the operation to a sidecar MemoryKunCache for the
duration of the outage. When false (default), exceptions
propagate. The fallback is per-process — replicas will not see
writes made while Redis is unreachable, which is the documented
tradeoff.

Consequences

Positive

Consumer services stop copy-pasting AddStackExchangeRedisCache +
JSON wrapper + TTL math.

A single upgrade point for cache-related features (SlidingExpiration
support, compression, multi-tier cache, metrics) — future work
lives in one module.

Kun.Caching.Tests exercises both backends under the same
contract, preventing silent drift between Memory and Redis.

Negative / Trade-offs

Any consumer host now carries a transitive dependency on
Microsoft.Extensions.Caching.StackExchangeRedis even when
UseMemory() is selected — the Redis package brings in
StackExchange.Redis (~1 MB trim-safe).

IKunCache.GetAsync<T> with a reference-type T returns null
for both "key absent" and "value was null when cached". Consumers
that need to distinguish should cache Option<T> / a tagged
envelope.

Risks

Risk	Mitigation
StackExchange.Redis AOT regression	CI AOT matrix includes Kun.Caching; Stop-gate if the analyzer warns.
Serializer drift between MemoryKunCache (no serialization) and RedisKunCache (JSON)	Contract tests in KunCacheBackendTests cover both backends with the same assertions — any divergence fails the matrix.
Per-key semaphore pool leaks under pathological unique-key usage	The pool is reference-counted; entries are removed on final release. Documented in AGENTS.md — callers with unbounded ephemeral keys should not use GetOrSetAsync.

Follow-ups

Migrate neuroagent-csharp services off hand-rolled
AddStackExchangeRedisCache to
services.AddKunCaching(...).UseRedis(...).

Source-generated JSON serializer example — demonstrate a
caller-supplied IKunCacheSerializer backed by a
JsonSerializerContext so AOT-strict consumers have a copy-paste
starting point.

Hybrid cache follow-on: once HybridCache GAs (expected .NET
10 GA), evaluate adding a UseHybrid(...) variant that keeps L1 in
process and writes L2 through to Redis — different single-flight
semantics.

Cache stampede metrics — surface cache.hit, cache.miss,
cache.stampede.single_flight_wait counters via the
ActivitySource pattern used by Kun.Mediator.

References

Handoff: task brief P1-KN-Caching

neuroagent-csharp/src/Services/*/Program.cs — the current
AddStackExchangeRedisCache registrations being abstracted

Kun.Audit / Kun.Storage / Kun.Observability — fluent-builder DI
pattern reused here

title: ADR-006: Introduce Kun.RateLimit Module
content:
本页镜像自 kun 仓库 docs/architecture/ADR-006-Kun.RateLimit-module.md（v2026.10.25）。Kun 文档与代码不一致处以代码为准（ADR-001 D1.8）；Qian 对 Kun 的选用与约束见与 Qian 的关系。改动请提到 kun 仓库。

Status: Accepted
Date: 2026-04-22
Author: claude-kun (Kun framework specialist)
Context: neuroagent-csharp/src/NeuroAgent.ServiceDefaults/Extensions.cs has been carrying an AddNeuroAgentRateLimiter helper that hand-wires AddRateLimiter(...) + AddPolicy("api", ...) + AddPolicy("auth", ...) with tenant / ip partitioning for each consumer service (P1-CS-RATELIMIT). Kun.Gateway ships its own YARP-oriented AddKunRateLimiter but that extension is hard-coded to a single kun-default policy with 100 req/min and is tightly coupled to the Gateway's partition resolver abstraction. Neither pattern serves non-gateway ASP.NET Core services that need named windows with different partitioning per window.

Decision

Introduce a new framework module Kun.RateLimit with a single entry
point:

services.AddKunRateLimit(opts =>
{
    opts.AddWindow("api", w =>
    {
        w.PermitLimit = 60;
        w.Period = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(1);
        w.PartitionKey = RateLimitPartitionKey.Tenant;
    });
    opts.AddWindow("auth", w =>
    {
        w.PermitLimit = 10;
        w.Period = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(1);
        w.PartitionKey = RateLimitPartitionKey.Ip;
    });
    opts.OnRejected = (ctx, ct) =>
    {
        // optional log / alert hook — response already committed
        return ValueTask.CompletedTask;
    };
});

The module owns:

KunRateLimitOptions — root options with a Dictionary<string, WindowRule>
of named windows and an optional OnRejected hook.

WindowRule — per-window: Period, PermitLimit, QueueLimit,
AutoReplenishment, and PartitionKey (enum).

RateLimitPartitionKey — closed-set enum: Tenant | User | Ip.
Keeps the API surface AOT-friendly (no open-set resolver interface
to register per-partition-source).

PartitionKeyResolver (internal) — maps enum + HttpContext to
partition string, with consistent fallbacks ("anonymous" /
"unknown").

AddKunRateLimit extension — translates the options into
AddRateLimiter(...) + one AddPolicy(name, partitioner-lambda)
call per window. Sets a global OnRejected that writes 429 +
Retry-After and invokes the consumer hook.

Module Shape and AOT

Property	Value
Layer	Infrastructure / Host-adjacent
FrameworkReference	Microsoft.AspNetCore.App (for Microsoft.AspNetCore.RateLimiting + System.Threading.RateLimiting)
<IsAotCandidate>	true — verified locally via dotnet publish -p:PublishAot=true /warnaserror up to the native-link stage. Zero analyzer warnings
Reflection	None. The AddPolicy overload used accepts a Func<HttpContext, RateLimitPartition<string>> lambda; AddPolicy<TPolicy> (DI-activated) is deliberately avoided

Alternatives Considered

Alternative	Why Rejected
A. Extend Kun.Gateway.AddKunRateLimiter	Gateway's extension is hard-coded to one policy and one IRateLimitPartitionResolver registration. Generalising it would bloat a host-layer module with concerns that belong in an Abstraction/Infrastructure module.
B. Reuse Kun.Gateway.IRateLimitPartitionResolver in a shared module	The resolver interface is open-set; every consumer that adds a new partition source (e.g. "API key") has to register a resolver impl. That's the wrong tradeoff for 95% of consumers who only want tenant / user / ip. The enum in this module captures the common cases directly.
C. Leave it in ServiceDefaults per consumer	That is the status quo being replaced; it cost neuroagent-csharp a redundant helper in every service with hard-coded limits.
D. New Kun.RateLimit module (selected)	Clean separation from the Gateway (which stays a YARP-specific host module); single-call registration for any ASP.NET Core service; closed-set partition enum keeps the API AOT-strict.

Design Notes

Fixed window, not sliding / token-bucket / concurrency. Matches
neuroagent-csharp's existing behaviour and what most HTTP APIs
actually want. Extending WindowRule with an Algorithm enum is a
follow-up once there is a concrete need.

Retry-After header always present on 429. The middleware
reads the lease's MetadataName.RetryAfter when available;
otherwise it falls back to the largest registered window's
Period. The caller always sees a usable hint.

OnRejected hook runs after the response is committed. Design
intent is logging / metrics / alerting, not response mutation.
Documented on the hook signature.

Partition enum, not open-set interface. Gateway keeps its own
IRateLimitPartitionResolver for per-route transforms; this module
keeps the ASP.NET Core endpoint surface clean.

Consequences

Positive

neuroagent-csharp's AddNeuroAgentRateLimiter can be replaced by a
three-line AddKunRateLimit(opts => ...).

Framework-level ergonomics: named windows match the .RequireRateLimiting("api")
decoration that ASP.NET Core already expects.

AOT-strict — another framework module that consumer hosts can pull
in without losing their AOT posture.

Negative / Trade-offs

Two rate-limit extensions in the framework now (Kun.Gateway.AddKunRateLimiter
for YARP, Kun.RateLimit.AddKunRateLimit for services). The
Kun.Gateway version is the narrower tool; it stays because YARP's
transform pipeline is different enough from endpoint rate limiting
that one size doesn't fit both.

Closed-set partition enum: consumers that need API-key partitioning
cannot plug one in without extending the enum in the framework.
This is a deliberate choice; revisit when a consumer requires it.

Risks

Risk	Mitigation
ASP.NET Core RateLimiting upgrade regresses AOT	CI AOT matrix includes Kun.RateLimit; stop-gate rule applies.
Consumer forgets app.UseRateLimiter() in the pipeline	Middleware is the consumer's responsibility — documented in AGENTS.md. Adding a UseKunRateLimit shim is a future-work item.

Follow-ups

Migrate neuroagent-csharp/ServiceDefaults off
AddNeuroAgentRateLimiter onto AddKunRateLimit.

Sliding / token-bucket variants: extend WindowRule with an
Algorithm enum when a consumer requires it; today's single
algorithm keeps the surface narrow.

UseKunRateLimit middleware shim for consumers that want to
call app.UseKunRateLimit() instead of UseRateLimiter().

Reconcile with Kun.Gateway.AddKunRateLimiter: once a real
consumer needs YARP + endpoint rate limits together, decide
whether to merge or keep them split.

References

Handoff: task brief P1-KN-RateLimit

neuroagent-csharp/src/NeuroAgent.ServiceDefaults/Extensions.cs —
AddNeuroAgentRateLimiter being abstracted

src/Kun.Gateway/RateLimiting/KunRateLimiterExtensions.cs — the
sibling YARP-specific extension that stays in place

title: ADR-007: Introduce Kun.MultiTenancy and Kun.MultiTenancy.EntityFrameworkCore Modules
content:
本页镜像自 kun 仓库 docs/architecture/ADR-007-Kun.MultiTenancy-module.md（v2026.10.25）。Kun 文档与代码不一致处以代码为准（ADR-001 D1.8）；Qian 对 Kun 的选用与约束见与 Qian 的关系。改动请提到 kun 仓库。

Status: Accepted
Date: 2026-04-22
Author: claude-kun (Kun framework specialist)
Context: The ITenantContext abstraction has lived in Kun.Core since day one, and Kun.EntityFrameworkCore.KunDbContext auto-applies a tenant global query filter in OnModelCreating. But the pieces that turn a JWT tid claim or X-Tenant-Id header into an ambient ITenantContext have so far been re-implemented in each consumer service — neuroagent-csharp/ServiceDefaults resolves from claims, Kun.Security.JwtTenantContext resolves per-request on HTTP, and Edge / Platform / Storage each register their own AddHttpContextAccessor + manual claim inspection. Similarly, the SaveChanges-time auto-fill that injects the current tenant on insert was not shipped with the framework; each consumer either forgets it or reimplements it.

Decision

Introduce two new framework modules, mirroring the
Kun.Audit + Kun.Audit.EntityFrameworkCore split:

Module	Layer	IsAotCandidate	Responsibility
Kun.MultiTenancy	Abstraction / Host-adjacent	true	ITenantResolver, DefaultTenantResolver (JWT / header / fallback), AsyncLocalTenantContext, TenantContextMiddleware, AddKunMultiTenancy / UseKunMultiTenancy DI
Kun.MultiTenancy.EntityFrameworkCore	Infrastructure	false	ApplyKunMultiTenantFilters ModelBuilder extension, KunTenantSaveChangesInterceptor auto-fill, IKunMultiTenantDbContext + KunMultiTenantModelCacheKeyFactory

The original handoff brief specified a single Kun.MultiTenancy
module with IsAotCandidate=true. That is incompatible with the
framework's layering rules: EF Core 10 is not AOT-strict (the
pre-existing Kun.EntityFrameworkCore runs trim-safe only), so
bundling the ModelBuilder extension + SaveChanges interceptor into an
AOT-candidate module would fail the CI AOT gate. Per the Stop-gate
rule (CLAUDE.md §Forbidden: do not silently flip IsAotCandidate),
the split is recorded here rather than bypassed.

Why the tenant filter lives in the framework, not the business layer

The brief's last bullet asks specifically for this — it is the core
design question and worth calling out:

Tenant isolation is a safety property, not a feature. A
query that accidentally escapes the filter is an incident. The
only way to stop it at a uniform standard is to apply the filter
globally at the framework's ORM seam, not ask every consumer to
remember.

The filter expression is mechanical. It is always
e.TenantId == tenantContext.TenantId; there is no per-module
variation that needs consumer code. Variation should live in the
tenant resolver (where there genuinely is variation: claim
name, header name, fallback), not in the filter.

The model-cache-key factory is non-obvious and load-bearing.
Without a per-tenant cache key, EF Core folds the filter
constant on first model build and silently leaks data across
tenants from that point on. Shipping
KunMultiTenantModelCacheKeyFactory with the framework closes
this hole for every consumer.

The interceptor is mechanical. Auto-filling TenantId on
insert is a single pattern repeated everywhere; leaving it to
business code means rows get written with empty tenant ids and
become invisible to subsequent reads under the filter.

The consumer stays in control of the policy — which JWT claim
name, which header, whether to use a "default" fallback, whether to
apply the filter at all. The mechanism is owned by the framework.

Module Shape

services.AddKunMultiTenancy(opts =>
{
    opts.UseJwtClaim("tid");                 // primary — S2S JWT
    opts.UseHttpHeader("X-Tenant-Id");       // fallback for admin tooling
    opts.FallbackTenantId = "default";       // last resort
});

services.AddDbContext<AppDbContext>((sp, opts) =>
{
    opts.UseNpgsql(connectionString)
        .AddInterceptors(sp.GetRequiredService<KunTenantSaveChangesInterceptor>())
        .ReplaceService<IModelCacheKeyFactory, KunMultiTenantModelCacheKeyFactory>();
});
services.AddKunMultiTenancyEntityFrameworkCore();

// In Program.cs:
app.UseAuthentication();
app.UseKunMultiTenancy();                    // AFTER auth, BEFORE endpoints
app.MapControllers();

// In AppDbContext:
protected override void OnModelCreating(ModelBuilder modelBuilder)
{
    base.OnModelCreating(modelBuilder);
    modelBuilder.ApplyKunMultiTenantFilters(this);
}

Kun.EntityFrameworkCore.KunDbContext already applies the filter
automatically and already exposes TenantIdForModelCacheKey; consumers
who inherit from it only need the AddKunMultiTenancy side and the
interceptor registration.

2026.10.12-hotfix.2 实现修正：非 KunDbContext 消费者实现 IKunMultiTenantDbContext，其 TenantIdForModelCacheKey 返回当前租户访问器的标识，并使用上面的 DbContext 重载。旧访问器重载已标记 KUNTENANT001 且在构建模型时明确拒绝；共享模型必须绑定当前执行上下文，迁移说明见 多租户安全文档。

Alternatives Considered

Alternative	Why Rejected
A. Single Kun.MultiTenancy module with IsAotCandidate=true (per brief text)	EF Core inside an AOT-strict module fails the CI gate. Stop-gate rule applies — opens this ADR instead.
B. Single module with IsAotCandidate=false	Forfeits AOT posture for consumers that only need the resolver + middleware (background workers, AOT-strict hosts without a DB).
C. Leave middleware + interceptor to consumers	That is the status quo being replaced. The SaveChanges auto-fill and the model-cache-key factory are load-bearing correctness features that every consumer would otherwise re-implement — or forget.
D. Split into Abstraction + Infrastructure (selected)	Matches the established Kun.Audit / Kun.Audit.EntityFrameworkCore pattern. AOT-strict consumers retain the resolver + middleware; EF consumers pick up the filter + interceptor in a sibling module.

Canonical tenant id type

Kun.Core.MultiTenancy.ITenantContext.TenantId has been string?
since day one, and IMultiTenant.TenantId is string?. The brief
mentions AsyncLocal<Guid?> and entity.TenantId == Guid.Empty; this
module keeps the string shape to preserve coherence with existing
types. The interceptor treats null or whitespace as "not yet
assigned" — a Guid-typed tenant would need to coerce through
Guid.TryParse at the resolver boundary anyway, and empty-GUID vs.
empty-string both read as "unset" to downstream code.

Consequences

Positive

neuroagent-csharp/ServiceDefaults sheds its hand-rolled claim
resolution, AddHttpContextAccessor registration, and the
per-service AsyncLocal plumbing.

KunMultiTenantModelCacheKeyFactory prevents a silent data-leak
hazard that every consumer would otherwise re-implement.

The SaveChanges interceptor guarantees that rows never land with
null / empty TenantId under normal flow — cutting down a whole
class of support tickets caused by "my data disappeared" reports.

Negative / Trade-offs

Two modules instead of one, tracking the Kun.Audit precedent.
Marginal overhead in release ceremony.

Consumers with a custom DbContext that does not inherit from
Kun.EntityFrameworkCore.KunDbContext must implement the
IKunMultiTenantDbContext interface to opt into per-tenant
model-cache partitioning. Documented on the interface.

The fallback tenant id pattern ("default") groups unauthenticated
traffic under one bucket. Consumers that want anonymous requests to
fall out of multi-tenant-filtered queries should set
FallbackTenantId = null — the filter then evaluates
e.TenantId == null, which returns rows explicitly flagged as
shared (or nothing at all).

Risks

Risk	Mitigation
OTel / EF Core upgrade regresses AOT on the main module	CI AOT matrix includes Kun.MultiTenancy; stop-gate rule applies.
Middleware runs before UseAuthentication() in a consumer's pipeline, resolver reads an empty ClaimsPrincipal	Documented in AGENTS.md; a future follow-up could add a startup-time validation that flags the ordering.
Consumer forgets ReplaceService<IModelCacheKeyFactory, KunMultiTenantModelCacheKeyFactory>	Filter silently folds on first tenant and leaks. Documented; a future follow-up could add a UseKunMultiTenancy() extension on DbContextOptionsBuilder that wires both the factory and the interceptor in one call.

Follow-ups

Migrate neuroagent-csharp/ServiceDefaults off its hand-rolled
tenant-resolution helper onto AddKunMultiTenancy.

UseKunMultiTenancy() on DbContextOptionsBuilder — a single
extension that wires both the interceptor and the
model-cache-key factory, reducing consumer ceremony.

Startup ordering validation — an IStartupFilter that flags
when UseKunMultiTenancy runs before UseAuthentication.

Subdomain / query-string resolver sources — extend
KunMultiTenancyOptions when a consumer requires them.

References

Handoff: task brief P1-KN-MultiTenancy

Kun.Core.MultiTenancy.ITenantContext / Kun.Core.Domain.IMultiTenant — the pre-existing contracts

Kun.EntityFrameworkCore.KunDbContext — the filter auto-application this module generalises

Kun.IntegrationTests/MultiTenancy/TenantFilterTests.cs — the per-tenant IModelCacheKeyFactory pattern this module ships framework-wide

Related ADR: ADR-003 (Kun.Audit module split for the same AOT / EF Core reason)
