title: ADR-008: Introduce Kun.Identity Module — Reversing ADR-001
content:
本页镜像自 kun 仓库 docs/architecture/ADR-008-Kun.Identity-module.md（v2026.10.25）。Kun 文档与代码不一致处以代码为准（ADR-001 D1.8）；Qian 对 Kun 的选用与约束见与 Qian 的关系。改动请提到 kun 仓库。

Implementation update (S1-KUN-004): the identity client guide and canonical S2S guide supersede the legacy issuer and incomplete cookie-flow examples below. The original rationale is retained as history.

Status: Accepted
Date: 2026-04-22
Author: claude-kun (Kun framework specialist)
Supersedes (partially): ADR-001 — Do Not Introduce a New Kun.Identity Module
Context: ADR-001 (Apr 2026) declined to create a Kun.Identity module because Phase 1 identity needs were fully covered by Kun.Gateway (OIDC → S2S JWT translation) and Kun.Security (S2S JWT validation + JWKS). That decision explicitly anticipated a revisit: "If future phases need cross-cutting identity abstractions (e.g., IPermissionChecker with policy store), we will revisit this ADR." Consumer-side divergence observed across three neuroagent-csharp services has now materialised exactly that signal.

What changed since ADR-001

Three concrete divergences drove the revisit:

Three near-duplicate AddJwtBearer configurations. neuroagent-csharp Edge, Platform, and Notification services each hand-roll services.AddAuthentication().AddJwtBearer(JwtBearerDefaults.AuthenticationScheme, opts => ...). The issuer / audience / JWKS URL pointing at Authentik is copied verbatim; the clock-skew and expiry-required flags differ slightly; each service reaches a subtly different security posture. The only way to pull these back into a single policy is a framework abstraction.

Per-service S2SJwtIssuer wiring. The existing Kun.Security.S2SJwt.S2SJwtIssuer exists as an implementation, but the public DI surface is verbose (services.AddOptions<S2SJwtOptions>()... + manual key loading). Consumers have been wrapping it with small adapter helpers — five different helpers, five different signatures.

OIDC code-exchange lives nowhere. Authentik supports both client-credentials (used by the gateway) and authorization-code flows. The code-flow exchange is not covered by either Kun.Gateway or Kun.Security today, so Edge open-coded an HttpClient.PostAsync against /application/o/token/ with inline form encoding. That code has drifted into five subtle variants across services.

The generalisable pattern — validate external tokens, mint S2S tokens, talk to an OIDC provider — is orthogonal to the gateway / security split. Lifting it to Kun.Identity consolidates all three configurations behind one fluent builder.

Decision

Introduce src/Kun.Identity/ (IsAotCandidate=true) exposing three
public abstractions and a single DI entry:

services.AddKunIdentity(id =>
{
    id.AddJwtBearer(opts => { opts.Issuer = ...; opts.Audience = ...; opts.JwksUri = ...; });
    id.AddS2SIssuer(opts => { opts.Issuer = ...; opts.SigningKeyPem = ...; });
    id.AddOidcClient("authentik", opts => { opts.Authority = ...; opts.ClientId = ...; opts.ClientSecret = ...; });
});

Abstraction	Purpose	Backing implementation
IJwtValidator	Validate external Bearer JWT → ClaimsPrincipal?	KunJwtValidator (JsonWebTokenHandler + ConfigurationManager<OpenIdConnectConfiguration> JWKS rotation)
IJwtIssuer	Mint signed JWTs (S2S flow)	KunJwtIssuer (RS256 via JsonWebTokenHandler + RsaSecurityKey)
IOidcClient	OIDC discovery + authorization_code exchange	KunOidcClient (HttpClient + source-gen JsonSerializerContext)

The module is a facade, not an IdP. It does not embed a token
database, does not sign user credentials, does not implement the
OIDC server role. Running Authentik / Keycloak / Auth0 remains the
consumer's responsibility; Kun.Identity gives them a uniform
client surface against that infrastructure.

Relationship to existing Kun.Security / Kun.Gateway

Kun.Security.S2SJwt (Issuer, Verifier, Options, JWKS middleware)
stays in place unchanged for backward compatibility. New services
prefer the Kun.Identity.IJwtIssuer / IJwtValidator surface
because it also covers external tokens and OIDC clients in one
registration — but existing consumers of Kun.Security.S2SJwt
keep working.

Kun.Gateway.S2sTokenIssuer remains the Gateway-internal S2S
issuer. A future refactor can have it implement
Kun.Identity.IJwtIssuer and delete the duplicate code path —
that migration is out of scope for this ADR.

Kun.Security.KunServiceAuthenticationExtensions.AddKunServiceAuthentication
is the ASP.NET Core AddJwtBearer pipeline wiring. It is not
subsumed here. Consumers that need ASP.NET Core's auth middleware
still call it; consumers that need framework-neutral bearer
validation (gRPC interceptors, background workers, custom
middleware) use IJwtValidator directly.

Why ADR-001 was right at the time, and is wrong now

ADR-001 weighed four drivers:

Driver	Still true today?
"Capability already exists" — Gateway + Security cover the lifecycle	Partially. They cover S2S, not external Bearer + OIDC code-flow.
"No gap in Phase 1"	No longer true. P1-CS-007 / P1-CS-010 shipped, and three consumer services now carry drift that a framework abstraction would eliminate.
"Avoid framework bloat"	Still a concern. This module adds ~9 types + two tests to the framework surface. The divergence cost exceeds that now.
"Downstream simplicity"	Inverted. Downstream is currently less simple because each service re-implements the same wiring.

The drivers that made ADR-001 correct at the time — Phase 1 scope,
no observed divergence, single pattern per service — are no longer
the situation. ADR-008 records the revisit with the exact signal
ADR-001 asked for.

Consequences

Positive

Consumer services replace per-repo auth helpers with one
AddKunIdentity(...) call — the divergence driver goes away.

IJwtValidator is framework-neutral; gRPC interceptors /
background workers can do bearer validation without spinning up
ASP.NET Core's auth pipeline.

OIDC code-exchange moves into the framework, closing the last
hand-rolled HttpClient.PostAsync against /token in consumer
code.

Negative / Trade-offs

Framework surface grows by one module (~9 public types).

Two S2S issuer implementations coexist until the
Kun.Security → Kun.Identity migration lands. Consumers picking
"which one" is mildly confusing until the canonical choice is
Kun.Identity.

The OIDC client only implements authorization-code grant. Refresh,
client-credentials, and device-flow are follow-ups.

Risks

Risk	Mitigation
Microsoft.IdentityModel upgrade regresses AOT	CI AOT matrix includes Kun.Identity; stop-gate rule applies.
Consumer mistakes IJwtIssuer for user-password auth	AGENTS.md is explicit: this module is an identity client, not an IdP.
Drift between Kun.Security.S2SJwtIssuer and Kun.Identity.KunJwtIssuer during the transition	Both use Microsoft.IdentityModel.Tokens primitives and the same JWS algorithm set; tests in Kun.Identity.Tests + Kun.Security.Tests cover round-trips on both sides.

Follow-ups

Migrate neuroagent-csharp services off their hand-rolled
AddAuthentication().AddJwtBearer helpers onto
AddKunIdentity(id => id.AddJwtBearer(...)).

Retire Edge's hand-rolled OIDC code exchange in favour of
IOidcClient.ExchangeCodeAsync.

Add refresh-token + client-credentials grants to
KunOidcClient once a consumer requires them.

Land the Kun.Security → Kun.Identity bridge: have
Kun.Security.S2SJwtIssuer implement Kun.Identity.IJwtIssuer
(or the reverse) so services can pick one canonical abstraction.

Consider IPermissionChecker — ADR-001 flagged this as the
specific trigger for a revisit. Still out of scope here; capture
in a future ADR when a second consumer needs it.

References

Handoff: task brief P1-KN-Identity

ADR-001 — the decision this ADR partially supersedes

Kun.Security/S2SJwt/* — existing S2S issuer / verifier that stays in place

Kun.Gateway/S2sTokenIssuer.cs — existing gateway-internal issuer, future follow-up to unify under Kun.Identity.IJwtIssuer

Microsoft.IdentityModel.JsonWebTokens.JsonWebTokenHandler — the AOT-clean 8.x primitive this module is built on

主体类型字段补充（S1-KUN-013）

ICurrentUser.PrincipalKind 属于当前身份的最小字段，来源是已经认证的 principal_kind claim，不是浏览器专有字段，也不是权限集合。依据当前身份扩展指南，字段放在已有 ICurrentUser 上，IAuthenticatedUser 继承，不增加第三个身份接口。

旧实现通过默认接口值 user 保持兼容；框架 JWT / Cookie 适配器保留真实类型，无类型声明的旧浏览器身份按 user。权限执行点接受 user/service/agent 的显式类型，歧义/未知值拒绝，不能把机器服务悄悄当作用户。Agent 仅保留其主体维度，不因此开放 S2S 签发。主身份的 sub 与 NameIdentifier 若同时存在须一致，关键 claim 不能从次身份补齐。

title: ADR-009: Introduce Kun.Configuration Module
content:
本页镜像自 kun 仓库 docs/architecture/ADR-009-Kun.Configuration-module.md（v2026.10.25）。Kun 文档与代码不一致处以代码为准（ADR-001 D1.8）；Qian 对 Kun 的选用与约束见与 Qian 的关系。改动请提到 kun 仓库。

Status: Accepted
Date: 2026-04-23
Author: claude-kun (Kun framework specialist)
Context: Every consumer service in neuroagent-csharp (Edge, Platform, Notification, Storage, Gateway) reads strongly-typed options from configuration, but the wiring has drifted across three patterns: Configure<T>(configuration.GetSection(...)) without any validation, hand-rolled IValidateOptions<T> implementations that miss cross-cutting attributes, and an inconsistent mix of [Required] from System.ComponentModel.DataAnnotations with .ValidateDataAnnotations() sometimes attached and sometimes not. The resulting failure modes at startup — silent defaults for missing secrets, runtime NullReferenceException on first use, or obscure "The field X is required" errors that don't say where X lives in appsettings.json — have cost operators real time.

Decision

Introduce src/Kun.Configuration/ (IsAotCandidate=true) with a
single DI entry point:

services.AddKunOptions<AuthentikOptions>("Authentik");

This wires in one call:

services.AddOptions<T>() — the Options builder.

.BindConfiguration("Authentik") — bind Authentik:* keys to T.

A custom IValidateOptions<T> (KunOptionsValidator<T>) that
runs DataAnnotations attributes plus any registered
IKunConfigurationValidator<T>, and prefixes every error with
the configured section path.

.ValidateOnStart() — IHostedService-driven fail-fast at host
start.

Plus three attributes tuned for configuration:

Attribute	Behaviour	Error shape
[RequiredConfig]	[Required] with AllowEmptyStrings = false.	'ClientId' is required but missing in configuration.
[UrlConfig]	Uri.TryCreate(value, UriKind.Absolute, ...); null accepted so callers can pair with [RequiredConfig].	'Authority' must be a valid absolute URL.
[NonEmptyStringConfig]	Rejects whitespace-only strings; null accepted so callers can pair with [RequiredConfig].	'ClientId' must be a non-empty string.

The failure messages surfaced by KunOptionsValidator<T> are
prefixed with the section path:

Authentik:ClientId — 'ClientId' is required but missing in configuration.
Authentik:Authority — 'Authority' must be a valid absolute URL.
Database:Primary:ConnectionString — 'ConnectionString' must be a non-empty string.

The operator now has the exact key to fix in appsettings.json.

Why DataAnnotations over FluentValidation

Dimension	DataAnnotations	FluentValidation
AOT posture	Reflection-based but quarantinable behind [RequiresUnreferencedCode] + [DynamicallyAccessedMembers(All)]	Entirely reflection-based; not AOT-clean without significant source-gen investment
API familiarity	Already used across neuroagent-csharp	Would add a new validator DSL for consumers to learn
Startup cost	Built into Microsoft.Extensions.Options.DataAnnotations	Additional package + scan
Cross-field rules	Custom ValidationAttribute works but is clunky	First-class

Primary path is DataAnnotations. The IKunConfigurationValidator<T>
interface is the escape hatch — consumers who need cross-field or
async validation implement it and register; KunOptionsValidator<T>
merges the results with DataAnnotations failures. If FluentValidation
demand materialises later, a Kun.Configuration.FluentValidation
adapter (sibling module) can register a FluentValidationConfigurator<T>
that implements the same interface — no change to the core.

Module Shape and AOT

Layer: Abstraction — depends only on Microsoft.Extensions.*
Options / Configuration / Hosting abstractions.

<IsAotCandidate>true</IsAotCandidate>. The AddKunOptions<T>
entry point is annotated with [RequiresUnreferencedCode] +
[RequiresDynamicCode] and the type parameter carries
[DynamicallyAccessedMembers(DynamicallyAccessedMemberTypes.All)]
so the trimmer preserves the properties DataAnnotations walks.
The Configuration-Binder source-generator diagnostics
SYSLIB1100/1101/1104 are suppressed in the csproj with a
targeted NoWarn — they fire on the unbounded-generic
BindConfiguration<TOptions> call by design, and the runtime
reflection fallback is the contract callers have already opted
into via the RequiresDynamicCode attribute.

If a future configuration-binder upgrade regresses the AOT
posture, stop-gate the upgrade; do not silently flip the
module to IsAotCandidate=false.

Alternatives Considered

Alternative	Why Rejected
A. Let every consumer call AddOptions<T>().BindConfiguration().ValidateDataAnnotations().ValidateOnStart() manually	That is the status quo being replaced — three drift paths have already been observed.
B. Skip DataAnnotations and build a bespoke validator interface	Would force consumers to learn a new validation idiom; loses the familiar [Required]/[Url] shape.
C. Adopt FluentValidation as the primary path	Not AOT-clean; extra dependency; new DSL to teach. Kept as a potential sibling module for the escape hatch.
D. DataAnnotations + IKunConfigurationValidator<T> escape hatch (selected)	Primary path covers 90% of cases in a familiar idiom; custom validator lets consumers add cross-field / async rules without fighting the framework.

Consequences

Positive

One-line fail-fast startup for typed options everywhere.

Error messages name the config path; operators stop triaging
"which ClientId?".

Framework-provided attributes (RequiredConfig, UrlConfig,
NonEmptyStringConfig) replace per-service helpers.

Custom cross-field validation remains possible via the escape
hatch.

Negative / Trade-offs

AddKunOptions<T> carries [RequiresUnreferencedCode] — AOT-strict
consumers propagate the attribute up the call chain or accept the
trim warning. Documented in AGENTS.md.

The NoWarn list suppresses real source-generator output that a
hypothetical future concrete-type API could avoid; acceptable
because AddKunOptions is the only public surface and its
reflection contract is explicit.

Risks

Risk	Mitigation
ConfigurationBinder / Options upgrade breaks the suppression shape	CI AOT matrix includes Kun.Configuration; stop-gate rule applies.
Consumer forgets to apply [DynamicallyAccessedMembers(All)] on a custom options type under AOT	The type-parameter annotation on AddKunOptions<T> propagates the constraint; callers get an analyzer warning at the call site.

Follow-ups

Migrate neuroagent-csharp/ServiceDefaults off hand-rolled
Configure<T>(GetSection(...)) onto AddKunOptions<T>.

FluentValidation adapter module (Kun.Configuration.FluentValidation)
if a second consumer needs cross-field / async rules that are
painful to express as attributes.

IOptionsMonitor<T> hot-reload validation — currently
ValidateOnStart runs once; hot-reload failures do not
re-trigger validation. If a consumer requires it, wire a
IOptionsChangeTokenSource<T> + re-run KunOptionsValidator<T>
on change.

References

Handoff: task brief P1-KN-Configuration

Microsoft.Extensions.Options.DataAnnotations — the underlying
library this module builds on

System.ComponentModel.DataAnnotations.ValidationAttribute — the
custom-attribute base

ADR-005 (Kun.Caching) — sibling example of an AOT-candidate
module with opt-in reflection via [RequiresUnreferencedCode]

title: ADR-010: Add Cookie Session + IAuthenticatedUser to Kun.Identity
content:
本页镜像自 kun 仓库 docs/architecture/ADR-010-Kun.Identity-cookie-session.md（v2026.10.25）。Kun 文档与代码不一致处以代码为准（ADR-001 D1.8）；Qian 对 Kun 的选用与约束见与 Qian 的关系。改动请提到 kun 仓库。

Implementation update (S1-KUN-004): the identity client guide and canonical S2S guide supersede the legacy issuer and incomplete cookie-flow examples below. The original rationale is retained as history.

Status: Accepted
Date: 2026-04-24
Author: claude-kun (Kun framework specialist)
Extends: ADR-008 — Introduce Kun.Identity Module
Supersedes: none
Context: neuroagent-csharp Edge and Platform each ship an /auth/callback?code=… endpoint that exchanges an Authentik OIDC code for tokens, drops them into an ASP.NET Core cookie, and restores HttpContext.User on subsequent requests. The OIDC exchange now lives behind Kun.Identity.IOidcClient (ADR-008) but the cookie session half is still hand-rolled per service — each service calls AddAuthentication(CookieAuthenticationDefaults.AuthenticationScheme) with subtly different options, invents its own ISessionStore-like shape (or worse, writes refresh tokens directly into the cookie), and exposes ICurrentUser via per-service adapters. The consumer drift ADR-008 was supposed to close is re-emerging one layer up.

What changed since ADR-008

Three concrete divergences drove this follow-up:

Three near-duplicate cookie registrations. Edge and Platform both
call services.AddAuthentication().AddCookie(...) with the same
Authentik issuer / audience / callback path, but with differing
ExpireTimeSpan, SlidingExpiration, Cookie.SameSite, and
Cookie.SecurePolicy values. None of them match the zero-trust
defaults the framework wants to enforce.

Session backend is whatever fits the demo. Edge keeps tokens in
the cookie payload (DataProtection-encrypted but large); Platform
writes a Dictionary<Guid, SessionRecord> into IMemoryCache and
calls it a session store. Neither is production-ready; neither
agrees with the other on eviction policy.

ICurrentUser is splintered. Kun.Core.Security.ICurrentUser
exposes UserId, Roles, IsAuthenticated — deliberately minimal,
because it was designed for S2S JWT claims. The cookie / browser
side needs TenantId (from the Authentik tenant claim),
Email, Name, and direct access to the request's
ClaimsPrincipal for downstream policy checks. Services currently
cast to an ad-hoc ICurrentUserEx type they each define.

ADR-008 consolidated external Bearer validation, S2S issuance, and
OIDC code exchange. The cookie session surface is the missing half of
the browser-facing flow.

Decision

Extend Kun.Identity with a cookie session surface and introduce a
new companion module Kun.Identity.AspNetCore for the ASP.NET
Core middleware wiring. The abstractions stay in the core
Kun.Identity package so non-ASP.NET-Core hosts (gRPC-only, worker
services that resume a session from a replayed request, integration
tests that fake the cookie layer) can target them without pulling the
ASP.NET Core dependency.

Abstractions added to Kun.Identity

// Kun.Identity/Abstractions/Session/ISessionStore.cs
public interface ISessionStore
{
    Task<SessionData?> GetAsync(string sessionId, CancellationToken ct = default);
    Task SetAsync(string sessionId, SessionData data, TimeSpan ttl, CancellationToken ct = default);
    Task DeleteAsync(string sessionId, CancellationToken ct = default);
}

public sealed record SessionData(
    string UserId,
    string? TenantId,
    string? Email,
    string? Name,
    IReadOnlyList<string> Roles,
    string AccessToken,
    string? RefreshToken,
    DateTimeOffset ExpiresAt);

// Kun.Identity/Abstractions/IAuthenticatedUser.cs
// Extension of Kun.Core.Security.ICurrentUser — not a replacement.
public interface IAuthenticatedUser : ICurrentUser
{
    string? TenantId { get; }
    string? Email { get; }
    string? Name { get; }
    ClaimsPrincipal? Principal { get; }
}

// Kun.Identity/Configuration/KunCookieAuthOptions.cs
public sealed class KunCookieAuthOptions
{
    public string CookieName { get; set; } = "kun.sid";
    public string? Domain { get; set; }
    public string Path { get; set; } = "/";
    public bool HttpOnly { get; set; } = true;
    public SameSiteMode SameSite { get; set; } = SameSiteMode.Lax;
    public CookieSecurePolicy Secure { get; set; } = CookieSecurePolicy.Always;
    public TimeSpan SessionTtl { get; set; } = TimeSpan.FromHours(8);
    public bool SlidingExpiration { get; set; } = true;
}

Implementations

Type	Module	Notes
InMemorySessionStore	Kun.Identity	Dev / tests. Per-process ConcurrentDictionary with TTL sweep on read.
RedisSessionStore	Kun.Identity	Depends on IKunCache (Kun.Caching). Uses the new reflection-free GetBytesAsync / SetBytesAsync overload (ADR pre-requisite landed on bd44a7f) so the generic [RequiresUnreferencedCode] path is avoided entirely. Payloads serialized via a source-generated SessionJsonContext. Key shape: kun:session:{sessionId}.
KunCurrentUser	Kun.Identity.AspNetCore	IAuthenticatedUser implementation resolved per-request from HttpContext.User.
UseKunCookieAuth middleware	Kun.Identity.AspNetCore	Reads the cookie → ISessionStore.GetAsync → populates HttpContext.User.
SignInHelper.SignInAsync	Kun.Identity.AspNetCore	Exchanges an OidcTokenResponse → writes SessionData → emits the cookie.
ChallengeHelper.BuildLoginRedirect	Kun.Identity.AspNetCore	Builds the /authorize redirect (PKCE) against the registered IOidcClient.

DI entry point

services.AddKunIdentity(id =>
{
    id.AddJwtBearer(...);                    // from ADR-008
    id.AddS2SIssuer(...);                    // from ADR-008
    id.AddOidcClient("authentik", ...);      // from ADR-008

    id.AddCookieSession(opts =>
    {
        opts.CookieName = "kun.sid";
        opts.SessionTtl = TimeSpan.FromHours(8);
        opts.UseRedisStore();    // default; swaps to .UseInMemoryStore() for tests/dev
    });
});

app.UseKunCookieAuth();

Module shape and AOT

Module	IsAotCandidate	Rationale
Kun.Identity	true (unchanged from ADR-008)	Session store implementations and the new abstractions are reflection-free; RedisSessionStore serializes through a source-generated SessionJsonContext.
Kun.Identity.AspNetCore (new)	true	Middleware touches HttpContext + ClaimsPrincipal (all BCL); no reflection, no JsonSerializer.Serialize(obj). AOT analyzer must stay clean; CI AOT matrix will include this module.

The IKunCache generic path stays out of the hot path. The
Redis-backed session store calls GetBytesAsync / SetBytesAsync
exclusively; the generic GetAsync<T> / SetAsync<T> methods retain
their [RequiresUnreferencedCode] / [RequiresDynamicCode]
annotations untouched. See commit bd44a7f for the caching-side
pre-requisite.

Why not put cookie middleware in Kun.AspNetCore?

Kun.AspNetCore today covers ProblemDetails, exception handling,
health checks, and endpoint routing helpers — cross-cutting concerns
that every Kun-hosted ASP.NET Core app wants. Cookie auth is
identity-scoped: it depends on ISessionStore, IOidcClient, the
KunIdentityBuilder, and the identity options graph. Mixing it into
Kun.AspNetCore would require that module to reference
Kun.Identity, which inverts the current dependency direction and
forces consumers that don't need auth to transitively drag identity
types into their closure.

A standalone Kun.Identity.AspNetCore keeps the layering clean:
Kun.Identity.AspNetCore → Kun.Identity → Kun.Core, with
Microsoft.AspNetCore.App as a framework reference only on the new
module.

Why extend ICurrentUser rather than change it?

Kun.Core.Security.ICurrentUser is shipped (listed in
Kun.Core/PublicAPI.Shipped.txt) and used by the gateway's S2S path,
the audit module's author resolution, and any consumer reading the
current user from a background worker. Adding TenantId / Email /
Principal there would be a breaking API change for every consumer
that implements the interface manually — and Kun.Core is a BCL-only
module that must not take a dependency on System.Security.Claims
in its public contract just to satisfy a cookie-flow concern.

IAuthenticatedUser : ICurrentUser is the minimum-surface extension:

S2S consumers keep using ICurrentUser and see nothing new.

Browser-flow consumers depend on IAuthenticatedUser explicitly,
receiving TenantId / Email / Name / Principal on top of the
existing fields.

The DI registration in Kun.Identity.AspNetCore registers
KunCurrentUser as the implementation of both
ICurrentUser and IAuthenticatedUser, so an endpoint can inject
either and get the same request-scoped instance.

This is a strict superset — no breaking change, no cast chains.

Consequences

Positive

Consumers replace per-repo cookie wiring with one .AddCookieSession(...)
call — the drift driver that ADR-008 closed for JWT / OIDC now
also closes for the cookie half.

RedisSessionStore is AOT-clean from day one because the serialization
hop goes through a source-generated JsonSerializerContext, not the
reflection-based IKunCacheSerializer default.

IAuthenticatedUser gives browser-flow endpoints a typed handle on
ClaimsPrincipal without forcing them to reach into HttpContext.User
directly.

Unblocks kimi's P0-AUTH-VERIFY — the consumer will call
id.AddCookieSession(...) + app.UseKunCookieAuth() rather than
re-implementing the wiring inside neuroagent-csharp/Identity/.

Negative / Trade-offs

Framework surface grows by one module (Kun.Identity.AspNetCore)
and ~6 public types (ISessionStore, SessionData,
IAuthenticatedUser, KunCookieAuthOptions, SignInHelper,
ChallengeHelper). The drift cost exceeds that.

Two session stores coexist (InMemory for tests/dev, Redis for
production). Consumers pick via fluent builder; the default when
neither is selected is in-memory with a one-time warning log
(consistent with Kun.Caching).

The Kun.Caching pre-requisite (byte[] overload) is a permanent
addition to IKunCache — callers other than Kun.Identity may
start reaching for it. That's acceptable: it's a narrower, more
AOT-friendly surface than the generic T path and the divergence
between "cached DTOs" (SetAsync<T>) and "cached blobs"
(SetBytesAsync) is intentional.

Risks

Risk	Mitigation
Cookie forgery / session fixation	KunCookieAuthOptions defaults: HttpOnly=true, Secure=Always, SameSite=Lax, cookie value is an opaque 256-bit session id, not a serialized token.
Redis outage drops every logged-in user	RedisSessionStore can opt into FallbackToMemoryOnRedisFailure on the underlying Kun.Caching options, matching the pattern other Redis-backed modules already follow. Document the trade-off in the module AGENTS.md.
Session TTL drift between cookie and store	SignInHelper writes the same SessionTtl into both the cookie max-age and ISessionStore.SetAsync ttl argument in one call site. Single source of truth.
Claims drift on token refresh	Refresh-token support is out of scope for this ADR; when it lands, SessionData.RefreshToken is already part of the record so the refresh path can update AccessToken / ExpiresAt without reshaping the session.

Follow-ups

Consume in neuroagent-csharp Edge + Platform — replace the hand-rolled
cookie registrations with AddCookieSession(...) + UseKunCookieAuth().
This is the P0-AUTH-VERIFY work that unblocks immediately after C5
of this task lands.

Add refresh-token rotation — KunOidcClient.ExchangeCodeAsync
already returns a RefreshToken; a future change can add a
background refresh on SessionData.ExpiresAt - skew. Out of scope here.

Sliding expiration edge cases — current SlidingExpiration = true
rewrites the cookie + Redis TTL on every authenticated request.
If telemetry shows this is too write-heavy on Redis, gate the
refresh by a configurable threshold (e.g. only rewrite when
remaining TTL < 50% of SessionTtl).

CSRF layer — cookies + browser flow need CSRF tokens; that's
a separate concern tracked by a future ADR once a second consumer
needs it. In the interim, consumers should wire
AddAntiforgery(...) explicitly.

References

Handoff: task brief P1-KN-Identity-CookieSession

ADR-008 — the decision this ADR extends

ADR-005 — the IKunCache contract the Redis store depends on

Kun.Core/Security/ICurrentUser.cs — the shipped base interface IAuthenticatedUser extends

Kun.Core/PublicAPI.Shipped.txt — the public-API commitment we avoid breaking by choosing extension over modification

Commit bd44a7f — feat(caching): add byte[] overload to IKunCache for session store (the AOT pre-requisite that made this ADR implementable without softening the IKunCache generic contract)

title: ADR-011: Result<T> composition extensions (sync + async)
content:
本页镜像自 kun 仓库 docs/architecture/ADR-011-Result-async-extensions.md（v2026.10.25）。Kun 文档与代码不一致处以代码为准（ADR-001 D1.8）；Qian 对 Kun 的选用与约束见与 Qian 的关系。改动请提到 kun 仓库。

Status: Accepted
Date: 2026-04-24
Author: claude-kun (Kun framework specialist)
Extends: none (first ADR dedicated to Kun.Core.Results)
Supersedes: none

Context: Kun.Core.Results.Result<T> ships today with only Ok / Fail
/ EnsureSuccess. Handlers that compose more than one step have to
hand-roll the short-circuit plumbing every time:

var user = await _userRepo.GetAsync(userId, ct);
if (user is null) return Error.NotFound("user.notFound", "User not found");

var policy = await _policy.EvaluateAsync(user, ct);
if (policy.IsFailure) return policy.Error;

var session = await _sessions.CreateAsync(user, ct);
if (session.IsFailure) return session.Error;

return Result<SessionDto>.Ok(MapToDto(session.Value));

neuroagent-csharp Edge, Platform, and the forthcoming gateway
handlers all repeat variants of this. The drift is exactly what
ADR-010 warned about for cookie sessions — the framework is
consumed as a dependency; every re-invented abstraction downstream
becomes a version skew in six months. Land the canonical
composition shape at the core.

Decision

Add extension methods on Kun.Core.Results.Result and
Kun.Core.Results.Result<T> covering the five canonical railway-
oriented operations — Map, Bind, Tap, Ensure, Match — in three
flavours:

Synchronous: extensions on Result / Result<T> receivers.

Asynchronous — Task<…> sources: extensions on
Task<Result> / Task<Result<T>> receivers so callers can
fluent-chain after await-producing calls.

Asynchronous — ValueTask<…> sources: extensions on
ValueTask<Result> / ValueTask<Result<T>> receivers for hot-
path handlers (Kun.Mediator pipeline, Saga step executors)
that return ValueTask to avoid Task allocation.

All extensions live in a new namespace-preserving file set under
src/Kun.Core/Results/. They are pure BCL — no new
<PackageReference> — per the Kun.Core zero-third-party-dep
rule.

Naming

Op	Signature sketch	Intent
Map<T, TOut>	Result<T> → Func<T, TOut> → Result<TOut>	Transform the success value; never fails
Bind<T, TOut>	Result<T> → Func<T, Result<TOut>> → Result<TOut>	Chain an op that can itself fail
Tap	Result<T> → Action<T> → Result<T> (pass-through)	Side effect on success, unchanged payload
Ensure	Result<T> → Func<T, bool> → Error → Result<T>	Add a post-condition; success with false predicate becomes the supplied Error
Match<T, TOut>	Result<T> → Func<T, TOut> → Func<Error, TOut> → TOut	Terminal fold into a single value

For the non-generic Result, only the pass-through ops apply
(Tap(Action), Ensure(Func<bool>, Error), Match<TOut>) plus a
Bind(Func<Result>) for sequencing side-effectful steps.

Async method names are the sync name + Async suffix:
MapAsync, BindAsync, TapAsync, EnsureAsync, MatchAsync.

Async overload matrix

For every async method on every source type:

Source	Delegate shape	CT?
Task<Result<T>>	sync Func<T, TOut>	no
Task<Result<T>>	async Func<T, CancellationToken, Task<TOut>>	yes
ValueTask<Result<T>>	sync Func<T, TOut>	no
ValueTask<Result<T>>	async Func<T, CancellationToken, ValueTask<TOut>>	yes

Rationale for exactly two delegate variants per (source × op)
cell:

The sync-delegate overload is essential because the common
downstream pattern is await RepoAsync() (returns
Task<Result<T>>) then a cheap pure transform (Map,
Ensure). Forcing callers into an async lambda for a sync
transform would add needless async/await state-machine
overhead.

The async-delegate overload with CancellationToken covers the
await → another await chain. The CancellationToken is
always the last parameter with a default so chained calls
that want to forward it can, and callers that don't need it
don't have to care.

Func<T, Task<TOut>> without CT is not added — if you have an
async delegate you should be accepting a CT. The compiler will
still bind to the CT-accepting overload with a throwaway
(_, _) => lambda, at the minor cost of explicit ceremony.

Return types

Sync ops on Result<T> return Result<TOut> or Result<T> per
the shape above.

Async ops on Task<Result<T>> sources return Task<Result<TOut>>
or Task<Result<T>>.

Async ops on ValueTask<Result<T>> sources return
ValueTask<Result<TOut>> or ValueTask<Result<T>>.

Keeping the return-type family aligned with the source type
preserves fluent chaining without forcing .AsTask() /
.AsValueTask() boundary friction.

Failure short-circuit semantics (normative)

On every op, if the input Result/Result<T> is in a failure
state, the delegate must not be invoked and the original
Error is carried through unchanged.

Ensure on a successful input invokes the predicate; if the
predicate returns false, the output becomes a failure carrying
the Error passed to Ensure. If the predicate returns true,
the input is passed through unchanged.

Match invokes exactly one of its two delegates — never both,
never neither.

CancellationToken semantics

Async overloads accept CancellationToken ct and forward it
unchanged to the supplied delegate.

Required, not optional. The sketch above intended
CancellationToken ct = default but the Roslyn PublicAPI analyzer
rule RS0026 ("Do not add multiple overloads with optional
parameters") flags that combination. Rather than suppress the rule
blanket-wide, the async-delegate overloads require an explicit CT;
callers who want no token pass default or
CancellationToken.None. The UX cost is small and the binary-
compat safety is concrete — future ADR revisions may revisit if a
pattern for safely suppressing RS0026 per-symbol emerges.

A pre-cancelled token surfaces OperationCanceledException via
the awaited delegate (or via CancellationToken.ThrowIfCancellationRequested()
where no delegate is called). We deliberately do not wrap
cancellation into a Result failure — cancellation is infra-
signal not business failure, matching the project rule
"exceptions are reserved for systemic failures".

AOT safety

All extensions are pure generic instantiation — no reflection, no
Expression trees, no MakeGenericMethod. Kun.Core stays
AOT-candidate (IsAotCandidate=true). The /warnaserror publish
verification step in the Executor's build gate is non-negotiable.

Public-API surface additions

Every new method is public static, XML-documented, and listed in
src/Kun.Core/PublicAPI.Unshipped.txt. Names above are normative
— any future rename requires an ADR that supersedes this one.

Alternatives considered

Then instead of Bind

F# / railway-oriented writeups often use Then (or andThen).
Rejected because .NET callers read Then as "do this next
unconditionally", which conflicts with Bind's
failure-short-circuit semantics. Bind is explicit about "only
runs on success" to anyone who has met the pattern before.

Select / SelectMany (LINQ syntax support)

Adding Select / SelectMany would unlock from … in syntax
for Result<T>. Rejected for this ADR: the LINQ sugar encourages
query-style composition that obscures the failure flow at the
call site. Handlers benefit from the explicit .Bind(…).Map(…)
chain — reviewers see where short-circuits happen. LINQ support
can be added later as a separate, opt-in namespace (using
Kun.Core.Results.Linq;) without breaking this ADR.

Single generic async source type via IResultSource<T>

A wrapper abstraction that erases Task vs ValueTask was
considered. Rejected: it adds a heap allocation on every call,
defeats AOT-friendliness of ValueTask, and introduces a new
type for consumers to learn. The 2× duplicate surface (Task +
ValueTask) is mechanical and the test matrix covers both.

Flatten (Result<Result<T>> → Result<T>)

Useful in combinator-heavy code; rejected as YAGNI for the
initial ADR. The common shape in handlers is Bind-and-done; no
observed case where a caller materialises Result<Result<T>>.
Revisit if a concrete consumer need appears.

Implicit Result-of-Result unwrapping inside Map

Would let Map double-duty as Bind when the transform returns a
Result<TOut>. Rejected: conflates two behaviours, makes the
compiler's overload resolution pick the wrong one on innocent
refactors, and requires runtime type inspection (breaks AOT).

Impact on existing code

No existing code changes — this ADR is purely additive.

neuroagent-csharp does not get migrated in this ADR's
scope. A follow-up ralplan will sweep hand-rolled patterns
after at least one -beta of Kun ships the extensions.

PublicAPI.Shipped.txt stays untouched; new methods are all in
PublicAPI.Unshipped.txt until the next release cut.

Kun.Mediator pipeline is a likely early internal consumer
(TracingBehavior / ValidationBehavior compose a chain of
failures today); migrating those behaviours is not in scope
for ADR-011 — also a follow-up.

Security / observability considerations

Extensions do not introduce logging, telemetry, or exception
translation paths. Kun.Observability / Kun.Grpc
interceptors continue to see Result<T> values and Errors
unchanged.

No claim data or tenant context flows through the extensions,
so they are tenant-agnostic and safe in any caller context.

Follow-ups

F1: Migrate neuroagent-csharp Edge / Platform handlers off
the hand-rolled pattern (separate P1 task, not self-managed).

F2: Evaluate LINQ Select / SelectMany in a separate
opt-in namespace once ADR-011 ships.

F3: Consider analyzer to flag if (result.IsFailure) return
result.Error; blocks where Bind / Map would be idiomatic —
likely YAGNI until migration data shows real drift.

title: ADR-012: Introduce Kun.Testing module
content:
本页镜像自 kun 仓库 docs/architecture/ADR-012-Kun.Testing-module.md（v2026.10.25）。Kun 文档与代码不一致处以代码为准（ADR-001 D1.8）；Qian 对 Kun 的选用与约束见与 Qian 的关系。改动请提到 kun 仓库。

Status: Accepted
Date: 2026-04-24
Author: claude-kun (Kun framework specialist)
Extends: none (first ADR dedicated to the testing tooling layer)
Supersedes: none

Context: Every tests/Kun.*.Tests project open-codes the same
shapes:

Assert.True(result.IsSuccess);
Assert.Equal("order.notFound", result.Error.Code);
Assert.Contains(order.DomainEvents, e => e is OrderPlacedEvent);

FluentAssertions is present, but Result<T> / IAggregateRoot are
not first-class shapes to it. So the same 3-line block gets retyped
in every test file. neuroagent-csharp tests show the same pattern.
ADR-010 warned about consumer drift at the session layer and ADR-011
fixed it at the Result composition layer — this ADR closes the
third obvious drift surface at the assertion layer.

Decision

Add a new top-level module Kun.Testing that exposes fluent
assertion helpers for Result / Result<T> and IAggregateRoot
domain-event collections. The module sits at the Abstraction
layer in the four-layer flow (depends on Kun.Core only, referenced
downward by consumer test projects).

Module placement

Host         : (no Kun.Testing here — tests consume, don't host)
Infrastructure: (no Kun.Testing here — test fixtures live in per-module Tests projects)
Abstraction  : Kun.Testing      ← NEW
Core         : Kun.Core

Kun.Testing is AOT-candidate (IsAotCandidate=true), packable
(IsPackable=true) so downstream services can consume it as a NuGet,
and carries no runtime <PackageReference> beyond Kun.Core. The
zero-third-party-dep discipline that guards Kun.Core extends one
hop up: testing helpers must not drag FluentAssertions, xUnit, or
any test-framework-specific API into consumer test projects' closure
against their will.

Framework-agnostic failure signalling

On assertion mismatch, helpers throw a dedicated
KunAssertionException : Exception (in namespace
Kun.Testing). Consumer test projects using xUnit, NUnit, or MSTest
all surface the throw as a test failure — the message is the
contract, not the exception type.

Rejected alternatives:

Throw Xunit.Sdk.XunitException: couples Kun.Testing to xUnit,
forcing NUnit/MSTest users to transitively depend on xunit.v3.

Throw FluentAssertions.Execution.AssertionFailedException: same
coupling problem, plus FluentAssertions 8.x switched to a paid
license which the consumer matrix does not uniformly accept.

Return bool: defeats the whole point — tests degrade to
Assert.True(result.ShouldBeSuccess()).

Surface

All helpers are public static extension methods. Namespaces:

Kun.Testing — KunAssertionException

Kun.Testing.Results — ResultAssertions

Kun.Testing.Domain — DomainEventAssertions

On Kun.Core.Results.Result / Result<T>:

Helper	Return	Throws if
ShouldBeSuccess()	void on Result, T on Result<T>	input is a failure
ShouldBeFailure()	Error	input is a success
ShouldHaveErrorCode(string code)	Error	input is success, or Error.Code ≠ code
ShouldHaveErrorType(ErrorType type)	Error	input is success, or Error.Type ≠ type

The T-returning ShouldBeSuccess on Result<T> lets callers chain
further assertions on the value: var user = result.ShouldBeSuccess();
user.Email.Should().Be("…");.

On Kun.Core.Domain.IAggregateRoot:

Helper	Return	Throws if
ShouldRaise<TEvent>()	TEvent	not exactly one TEvent in DomainEvents
ShouldRaiseExactly<TEvent>(int count)	IReadOnlyList<TEvent>	DomainEvents.OfType<TEvent>().Count() ≠ count
ShouldNotRaise<TEvent>()	void	any TEvent present

Using OfType<TEvent>() + LINQ is compile-time safe and AOT-friendly
— no reflection, no MakeGenericMethod. The type-parameter-erasure
that AOT forbids lives in Type.GetMethod, not in generic extension
methods.

Error-message contract

Every KunAssertionException message must contain:

The helper name (ShouldBeSuccess, ShouldRaise<T>, …).

What was expected (the T, string code, int count).

What was actually seen (the actual Error.Code, the actual
event-type list, …).

Example:

ShouldRaise<OrderPlacedEvent> — expected exactly 1 but saw 0 event(s) of that type. Actual events: [OrderDraftedEvent, OrderLineAddedEvent].

Downstream test output — regardless of framework — then carries the
information a reviewer needs without spelunking into source.

What is not in scope

Outbox assertions (outbox.ShouldContain("order.placed.v1")).
OutboxMessage lives in Kun.EntityFrameworkCore, which is
explicitly non-AOT (EF Core forces it). Adding a reference from
Kun.Testing to Kun.EntityFrameworkCore would drag EF Core into
every consumer of the testing helpers. Tracked as a future
Kun.Testing.EntityFrameworkCore companion module — ships only if
a consumer shows concrete demand.

Testcontainers / DB fixtures: per-module Tests projects bring
their own. Kun.Testing is AOT-candidate and pure; fixtures pull
Docker.

ASP.NET Core test server wrappers (WebApplicationFactory<T>):
belongs in a different module if needed. Non-AOT by construction.

Integration-event assertions on IntegrationEvent: shares the
Outbox-scope logic; deferred for the same reason.

Adoption strategy

Smoke-adopt in tests/Kun.Core.Tests only during the KN-SELF-002
implementation — 3–5 call sites, not a mass convert, to prove the
dependency shape works.

Other tests/Kun.*.Tests and neuroagent-csharp tests migrate
lazily — no repo-wide sweep planned. The ADR sets the default;
callers converge naturally when they touch each file.

No version cadence promise: Kun.Testing rides the same -beta /
stable release cycle as the rest of the framework.

Alternatives considered

Put helpers inside Kun.Core

Rejected. Kun.Core is the framework's runtime seed; adding
assertion helpers there would (a) bloat the NuGet package shipped to
production services and (b) mix runtime and test-only surfaces,
which obscures reviews ("is this used in prod?"). Separation is
cheap when the types live at the same abstraction level.

Put helpers inside each Kun.*.Tests project

Rejected — this is exactly the status quo we're replacing. Each
Tests project reinvents the wheel.

Build on top of FluentAssertions by shipping custom

Should() extensions

Rejected. FluentAssertions 8.x is a paid library; propagating a
forced dependency to consumer test projects is not acceptable. Our
own surface is small (≤12 helpers) and doesn't need the extension
machinery.

Source generator that emits assertion extensions

Interesting but large scope for the value it unlocks. Parked. The
hand-written surface is tiny; generators would win only if the
surface balloons to dozens of helpers.

Use System.Diagnostics.Contracts.Contract.Assert

Contract.Assert throws ContractException which is internal-ish
and not visible on the public API surface. Bad UX for test output.

Security / observability considerations

Helpers never log or emit telemetry — they throw synchronously.

No claim data or tenant context flows through. Safe in any caller.

The KunAssertionException.Message string is the only side-effect
visible to test runners; helpers pass-through the original
Error object on the returning variants without copying or
mutating.

AOT safety

Zero reflection. Generic extension methods with T constraints
resolve at compile time.

OfType<T>() materialises via sequence filtering — no IL3050.

No Expression trees, no MakeGenericMethod, no Activator.

Kun.Testing.csproj sets <IsAotCandidate>true</IsAotCandidate>;
Directory.Build.props then wires IsAotCompatible,
IsTrimmable, and the trim/AOT/single-file analyzers.

Impact on existing code

Purely additive. No existing test file changes except the 3–5 smoke-
adoption sites in tests/Kun.Core.Tests (which should remain
trivially reversible — each site still compiles with the old
Assert.* form if Kun.Testing is removed).

Follow-ups

F1: Companion Kun.Testing.EntityFrameworkCore module for
Outbox / KunDbContext assertions if demand surfaces.

F2: Mass-adopt sweep across tests/Kun.*.Tests projects after
KN-SELF-002 ships — possibly delegated to a claude-kun follow-up
self-managed task (KN-SELF-xxx).

F3: neuroagent-csharp adoption tracked separately as a P1
task if tests drift persists.

Source generator that emits assertion extensions

title: ADR-013: Baggage-driven activity enricher for Kun.Observability
content:
本页镜像自 kun 仓库 docs/architecture/ADR-013-Kun.Observability-enricher.md（v2026.10.25）。Kun 文档与代码不一致处以代码为准（ADR-001 D1.8）；Qian 对 Kun 的选用与约束见与 Qian 的关系。改动请提到 kun 仓库。

Status: Accepted
Date: 2026-04-24
Author: claude-kun (Kun framework specialist)
Extends: ADR-004 — Kun.Observability module decision
Supersedes: none

Context: KunActivitySources pre-registers the four framework
sources (Kun.Mediator, Kun.EventBus.Outbox, Kun.Grpc,
Kun.Saga). Spans from those sources reach the Aspire / Jaeger UI
correctly, but carry no tenant.id / user.id tags. Operators
filtering by tenant or correlating spans to application logs end up
doing the join by hand every time. The information exists —
ITenantContext knows the tenant, ICurrentUser knows the user, the
Outbox envelope carries a message_id — but there's no wired path
from those sources to span tags.

Decision

Read enrichment values from OpenTelemetry baggage rather than
from scoped DI services, and mirror a whitelisted set of baggage
keys onto span tags at Activity start time via a
BaseProcessor<Activity> registered into the TracerProviderBuilder.

Consumer code that has tenant/user/outbox info pushes the values into
baggage once (usually at the request entry point — Kun.Gateway
already does this for the S2S JWT tenant claim via an
IEndpointFilter), and the baggage rides the ambient
AsyncLocal<>-backed context across HTTP / gRPC / async hops,
reaching every downstream Activity without additional wiring.

Hook point: OnEnd, not OnStart

The mirror happens in BaseProcessor<Activity>.OnEnd, not
OnStart. Rationale — OnStart runs the instant Activity.Start()
is called, which is before consumer code inside the activity
body has a chance to call SetBaggage on it. OnEnd runs just
before the activity leaves the pipeline toward exporters and sees
every baggage entry that was set at any point in the activity's
lifespan. This handles both idiomatic cases cleanly:

Baggage set at request boundary → child activity inherits it →
OnEnd mirrors it to tags.

Baggage set mid-activity (less common but legal) → OnEnd still
sees the final baggage state and mirrors it.

Exporters receive the tagged activity on the same pipeline pass
because OnEnd precedes the exporter call in OTel's processor
chain.

Why baggage and not scoped DI

The intuitive design — "processor constructor takes
IServiceProvider, resolves ITenantContext on each OnStart" —
breaks for three reasons:

BaseProcessor<Activity> instances are singletons in the OTel
pipeline. Resolving scoped services from the root provider
throws at runtime.

Even with IServiceScopeFactory, the processor has no way to
know which scope to resolve against. The activity being
started may have been queued by a background service whose scope
closed before the activity reaches the exporter.

Background contexts (Saga executor, Outbox publisher, timers)
either have no DI scope or have a different scope than the
originating request. Trying to thread the "right" scope through
every activity-emitting code path is exactly the hand-stitching
this ADR is meant to eliminate.

Baggage sidesteps all three. It is the W3C-standard async-propagated
context slot. Activity.Current?.Baggage is always accessible, no
DI needed, no lifetime confusion.

Canonical baggage keys

public static class KunBaggageKeys
{
    public const string TenantId         = "tenant.id";
    public const string UserId           = "user.id";
    public const string OutboxMessageId  = "outbox.message_id";
}

Names follow OpenTelemetry semconv naming (namespace.attribute).
Other baggage keys present on the activity are ignored — the
processor copies only the whitelisted set. Consumers that want
additional tags add them at the code site that already has the
value; they do not register a new enricher.

Default posture: opt-in

New flag KunObservabilityOptions.EnrichActivitiesFromBaggage,
default false. Two reasons for opt-in:

Adds a processor to the tracing pipeline and thus a few
nanoseconds per span. Negligible in practice but we keep
observability features additive and measurable.

Baggage can carry values a downstream operator did not expect to
see exported (e.g., sensitive PII a consumer service pushed in a
custom key). Although this processor copies only the whitelisted
keys, explicit opt-in forces callers to think about the baggage
contract their service is producing.

Downstream services enable the flag in their
builder.Services.AddKunObservability(o => o.EnrichActivitiesFromBaggage = true)
call.

Processor scope

The processor operates only on activities whose ActivitySource.Name
is in KunActivitySources.All — framework-owned spans. ASP.NET Core
/ HttpClient / EF Core instrumentation spans are handled by their
respective built-in enrichers and should not be touched by this one.

AOT safety

BaseProcessor<Activity> is an abstract class with no generic
constraints; extending it is AOT-safe. Activity.Baggage returns a
non-generic IEnumerable<KeyValuePair<string, string?>> which
materialises via the BCL without reflection. No MakeGenericType,
no Expression trees. The existing
<IsAotCandidate>true</IsAotCandidate> on Kun.Observability stays
unchanged.

What it is not

Not a log-record enricher. OpenTelemetry.Logs.LogRecord has a
separate AttributeEnricher surface — that's F1.

Not a metric-dimension enricher. Most Kun metrics are counters
without labels today; adding dimensions is premature. F-out.

Not a replacement for explicit, code-site tagging. Handlers
that know they just processed a specific resource (order.id,
saga.instance_id) should still call
Activity.Current?.SetTag("order.id", id) at the site — baggage
is for cross-cutting dimensions, not per-entity identifiers.

Alternatives considered

Capture IServiceScopeFactory and resolve per-activity

Rejected — see §Why baggage and not scoped DI above. The scope
uncertainty makes this design incorrect for background-issued
activities.

ActivityListener registered globally

Equivalent capability but ActivityListener is less structured than
a BaseProcessor and cannot participate cleanly in the
TracerProviderBuilder lifecycle; two callbacks (ActivityStarted,
ActivityStopped) duplicate the BaseProcessor model without
benefit. Chose BaseProcessor<Activity> for consistency with the
rest of the OTel SDK wiring.

Force every framework component to call Activity.SetTag

Rejected. That's exactly the "Mediator behaviour / Outbox publisher /
Saga executor / Grpc interceptor all know how to tag tenant_id"
hand-stitching we're replacing. Any future activity-emitting site
would have to remember the incantation.

Full IKunActivityEnricher pluggable interface + registry

Considered as a larger surface. Rejected for this ADR's scope — the
built-in baggage-to-tags mapper covers the known need; adding a
pluggable enricher abstraction should wait until a concrete second
implementation appears. YAGNI, revisit if consumer service demands a
custom enricher that can't be expressed as "push this value into
baggage".

Follow-ups

F1 — Resolved 2026-04-24 (KN-SELF-006): Log-record enricher
that mirrors the same baggage keys onto LogRecord.Attributes.
See §F1 resolution below.

F2: Expose baggage-tagging demo in Kun.Sample.AppHost
Aspire dashboard when the samples move beyond placeholder.

F3: If a concrete consumer need surfaces for a non-baggage
enrichment source (e.g., reading from a distributed cache or an
S2S JWT without baggage plumbing), promote to a pluggable
IKunActivityEnricher abstraction. Until then, this ADR is the
complete surface.

Impact on existing code

Purely additive. AddKunObservability gains one optional flag
(default off). Kun.Observability.csproj takes no new
PackageReference. Existing Aspire / OTLP pipelines remain
unchanged for consumers that do not flip the opt-in flag.

§F1 resolution (2026-04-24, KN-SELF-006) — log-record enricher

Span enrichment alone still forces operators to join spans ↔ logs
by hand (e.g. tenant.id filter works in the Aspire trace UI but
not in its log tab). KN-SELF-006 closes the loop by shipping a
companion KunBaggageLogRecordProcessor that mirrors the same
whitelisted baggage subset onto LogRecord.Attributes.

Shape, in one paragraph

Internal BaseProcessor<LogRecord> hooked at OnEnd. Reads
Activity.Current?.Baggage (logs, unlike activities, do not
auto-carry baggage; baggage lives on the ambient
Activity.Current instead). For each key in KunBaggageKeys.All
that is present on baggage, add it as a LogRecord attribute
if the attribute is not already there. Never overwrite a
consumer-set attribute: the log statement's own tenant.id=…
call wins.

Why OnEnd, not OnStart

Same reason as the span enricher (see §Hook point above) — the
ambient state we care about is finalised at OnEnd, not when the
log call first enters the processor chain.

Why "add if missing" instead of "overwrite"

A LogRecord that already carries tenant.id either came from
(a) a consumer-written log statement that deliberately set a
per-entity tenant for that record, or (b) an earlier instrumentation
pipeline. In both cases overwriting would surprise the author of
the log call. The enricher defers to the explicit set.

Opt-in flag

New KunObservabilityOptions.EnrichLogsFromBaggage (default
false). Mirrors the posture of EnrichActivitiesFromBaggage —
explicit flip forces consumers to think about what baggage contract
their service produces.

Tests

tests/Kun.Observability.Tests/LogBaggageEnrichmentTests.cs
covers: baggage-present → attribute mirrored; flag off → no mirror;
log-statement already set the key → kept; no Activity.Current →
no crash, no attrs added.

AOT safety

BaseProcessor<LogRecord> + Activity.Baggage enumeration + the
LogRecord attribute API are all reflection-free. Kun.Observability
keeps IsAotCandidate=true; ILC pass stays 0-warning.

title: ADR-014: Result-returning validation pipeline behavior
content:
本页镜像自 kun 仓库 docs/architecture/ADR-014-Validation-Result-behavior.md（v2026.10.25）。Kun 文档与代码不一致处以代码为准（ADR-001 D1.8）；Qian 对 Kun 的选用与约束见与 Qian 的关系。改动请提到 kun 仓库。

Status: Accepted
Date: 2026-04-24
Author: claude-kun (Kun framework specialist)
Extends: ADR-011 — consumer
of the Result<T> composition surface.
Supersedes: none

Context: src/Kun.Validation/Behaviors/ValidationPipelineBehavior.cs
is the exception-throwing validator pipeline behavior: any
validator error turns into ValidationException. That matches how
validators in most .NET codebases have historically worked, but it
conflicts with the Kun-wide rule in kun/CLAUDE.md
§Architectural constraints:

Business failures use Result / Result<T>, not exceptions.

Handlers that return Result<T> still have to sit behind a
try/catch for ValidationException at every call site, or trust
ASP.NET / gRPC middleware to translate the exception — both of
which mask the failure at the handler-composition layer ADR-011
tried to make ergonomic.

The throwing behavior's own XML doc already called this out:

For Result-based semantics (returning
Result.Fail(Error.Validation(...)) instead of throwing), compose
this behavior inside a user-written "ValidationResultAdapter"
behavior — shipped as a follow-up.

KN-SELF-007 is that follow-up.

Decision

Ship a second pipeline behavior,
ValidationResultPipelineBehavior<TRequest, TValue>, that runs the
validators in the same loop the throwing variant uses but on
aggregated errors returns Result<TValue>.Fail(Error.Validation(
"request.invalid", …)) instead of throwing. Handlers downstream
never see an exception for business-validation failures.

Scope — Result<TValue> only

Only the generic Result<TValue> variant ships in this task. The
non-generic Result variant (for commands with no return value) is
deliberately out of scope:

Most Kun handlers return a value. The dominant pattern is
IRequest<Result<OrderDto>>, not IRequest<Result>.

Adding the non-generic variant doubles the DI-registration
surface (one helper per constrained TResponse).

Void-returning commands keep working with the throwing
ValidationPipelineBehavior; the exception-path cost is
acceptable for a small minority.

Tracked as F1 below.

DI registration — explicit, per request type

A behavior constrained as
IPipelineBehavior<TRequest, Result<TValue>> where TRequest :
IRequest<Result<TValue>> cannot be registered as an open-generic
against the full IPipelineBehavior<,> surface — the DI container
would try to close it for every (TRequest, TResponse) pair and
hit a runtime type-system failure for non-Result responses.

Instead, consumers register per request type:

services.AddKunMediator(mediator =>
{
    mediator
        .AddValidator<CreateOrderCommand, CreateOrderValidator>()
        .AddValidationResultBehavior<CreateOrderCommand, OrderDto>();
});

This mirrors the existing
AddValidator<TRequest, TValidator>() pattern — explicit,
greppable, AOT-safe.

Coexistence with the throwing variant

Consumers pick one or the other per request type. Registering
both behaviors for the same TRequest would result in
non-deterministic order-dependent behavior (first one in the pipeline
wins; the second runs on the already-converted result). We do not
ship a runtime diagnostic for this misconfiguration because:

Detecting it cleanly would require enumerating all registered
pipeline behaviors at Mediator build time — not currently a public
hook.

The misconfiguration is rare and loud once it occurs (double-wrapped
validation messages stand out).

Doc guardrail only — src/Kun.Validation/AGENTS.md gets a "Result vs
exception" subsection pointing at this ADR.

Error shape

Aggregated ValidationError.Message strings are joined with "; "
into the Error.Message. Error.Code is the constant
"request.invalid". Consumers who need structured error payloads
(per-field error dicts) can post-process the returned Result via
ADR-011 .Match / .Bind — the framework does not ship a second
Error shape per validator, because the dominant consumer behavior
(gRPC 400, HTTP 400 JSON body) is already served.

AOT safety

No reflection. typeof(Result<TValue>) is compile-time-known per
closed generic.

Error.Validation and Result<TValue>.Fail are pure BCL — no
source-generator dependency.

The validator loop is the same shape the throwing variant uses
and has been AOT-green since Kun.Validation shipped as
IsAotCandidate=true.

Alternatives considered

One behavior that catches ValidationException and converts

Catch the existing exception and translate to Result.Fail. Works
without requiring a separate behavior but keeps the
throw-and-catch overhead (allocating the exception, building its
stack trace). Rejected — defeats the performance argument for using
Result and hides the conversion from code review.

Open-generic DI registration with a runtime type check

Register IPipelineBehavior<,> → ValidationResultPipelineBehavior<,>
and have the behavior short-circuit when TResponse isn't
Result<T>. Rejected — type-system constraints at the registration
level are cleaner than behavior-body runtime checks, and consumer
code composing the pipeline would silently skip validation for any
misregistered closure.

Modify the existing throwing behavior in place

Change the current ValidationPipelineBehavior to return Result
when the response type matches, throw otherwise. Rejected — silent
behavioural change to an already-shipped extension surface; would
require a CHANGELOG breaking note and a migration guide. Much
safer to ship a sibling behavior.

Provide a source generator that emits a registration per handler

Scan the assembly for IRequestHandler<*, Result<*>> and register
the right behavior closure. Rejected for this ADR — source
generators are deferred Kun-wide per docs/roadmap.md §环境与流程类
until M5 post-review. The explicit AddValidationResultBehavior
extension is the short-term surface; an SG can wrap it later.

Follow-ups

F1: Non-generic Result variant —
ValidationResultPipelineBehavior<TRequest> for
IRequest<Result>. Resolved 2026-04-24 (KN-SELF-012) —
shipped as a sibling class in the same file as the generic
variant, registered via the single-type-param overload
AddValidationResultBehavior<TRequest>() on KunMediatorBuilder.
The "doubled registration surface" concern from §Scope
(Result<TValue> only) turned out to be a single DI-extension
overload; the per-request-type explicit-registration pattern
was already the dominant surface, so the incremental cost
was small.

F2: Structured error payload (Error.Validation subtype
carrying a per-field error dict). Defer until consumers have a
concrete need past the joined-message default.

F3: Convenience extension that registers the behavior for
every IRequestHandler<*, Result<*>> discovered in an assembly.
Requires source generator — see Alternatives §Modify-existing.

Impact on existing code

Purely additive. The existing throwing
ValidationPipelineBehavior is untouched. Consumers not opting in
see no change. Kun.Validation.csproj gains no new
PackageReference.

toc.text: DI registration — explicit, per request type
One behavior that catches `ValidationException` and converts
Open-generic DI registration with a runtime type check
Modify the existing throwing behavior in place
Provide a source generator that emits a registration per handler

title: ADR-015: Outbox pattern design for Kun.EventBus
content:
本页镜像自 kun 仓库 docs/architecture/ADR-015-Outbox-pattern.md（v2026.10.25）。Kun 文档与代码不一致处以代码为准（ADR-001 D1.8）；Qian 对 Kun 的选用与约束见与 Qian 的关系。改动请提到 kun 仓库。

Status: Accepted (retroactive)
Date: 2026-04-24
Author: claude-kun (Kun framework specialist)
Extends: docs/architecture/why-outbox.md (primer)
Supersedes: none

Context: Integration events fan out to downstream services over
RabbitMQ. A naive implementation publishes during the write-side
handler — which either (a) publishes before commit (downstream sees
an event for a state that never existed if the transaction rolls
back), or (b) publishes after commit (downstream never sees an
event if the app crashes between SaveChanges and Publish). The
Outbox pattern closes both failure modes by persisting a message
row inside the write transaction and publishing asynchronously.

Kun ships the pattern end-to-end, but the rollout predates the ADR
index. kun/CLAUDE.md §Outbox has the normative rules; this ADR
walks through the design so new contributors can reason about the
type surface without reverse-engineering it.

Decision

Type surface

All abstractions live in Kun.EventBus; the persistence half
lives in Kun.EntityFrameworkCore. Two modules because:

Kun.EventBus must stay AOT-candidate and take no EF Core
dependency — the publisher loop and the consumer idempotency
machinery do not need EF Core.

Kun.EntityFrameworkCore is the one place we accept non-AOT
trade-offs (ADR-004 trail), and atomic enqueue+save has to
run inside DbContext.SaveChangesAsync.

Namespace / type	Role
Kun.EventBus.Outbox.OutboxMessage	Persisted row: Id, EventTypeId, Payload, Status, TraceParent, TraceState, retry counters.
Kun.EventBus.Outbox.OutboxStatus	Pending / Published / Failed. Enum.
Kun.EventBus.Outbox.IIntegrationEventOutbox	Consumer-facing append API: EnqueueAsync(IIntegrationEvent, CancellationToken). Called from handler code.
Kun.EventBus.Outbox.IOutboxWriter	Low-level write primitive — used by the EF Core accumulator and by any hand-rolled IIntegrationEventOutbox implementation.
Kun.EventBus.Background.IOutboxMessageStore	Read / update store the publisher pump talks to (ReadPendingBatchAsync, MarkPublishedAsync, MarkFailedAsync).
Kun.EventBus.Background.IOutboxLockProvider	Distributed lease so multiple pods don't double-publish. TryAcquireAsync(lockName, ttl, ct) returns IAsyncDisposable?; null means another instance holds it.
Kun.EventBus.Background.OutboxPublisherBackgroundService	Hosted service running the read → lock → publish → mark loop.
Kun.EventBus.Background.OutboxPublisherOptions	Batch size, poll interval, lease TTL, failure backoff.
Kun.EventBus.Background.NullOutboxLockProvider	Explicit single-pod opt-in only — never the production default.
Kun.EventBus.Background.RedisOutboxLockProvider	Multi-pod production default — SET NX + EX.
Kun.EventBus.Background.Internal.ProcessedMessageStore	Consumer-side "seen before?" cache backing IdempotentConsumerDecorator<T> (ADR-003 trail).
Kun.EntityFrameworkCore.IntegrationEventOutboxAccumulator	Collects aggregate-produced IIntegrationEvents during SaveChangesAsync and writes OutboxMessage rows in the same transaction.
Kun.EntityFrameworkCore.OutboxMessageConfiguration	IEntityTypeConfiguration<OutboxMessage> — table name, column types, partial index on Status = Pending + CreatedAt ordering.

Atomicity boundary

The contract is: Outbox enqueue + aggregate save commit together
or neither. Enforced by
IntegrationEventOutboxAccumulator.AccumulateBeforeSave hooked into
KunDbContext.SaveChangesAsync:

ChangeTracker.Entries<IAggregateRoot>() gives all tracked
aggregates.

For each, drain DomainEvents → convert to IIntegrationEvent
via the domain-event handler chain → materialise as
OutboxMessage rows on the same DbContext.

ClearDomainEvents() on every aggregate so replay doesn't
double-enqueue.

The single SaveChangesAsync call writes both aggregate changes
and outbox rows in one EF Core transaction.

There is no "open transaction, publish, commit, close" dance.
The publish is asynchronous and happens in a separate process
(background service), decoupled from the write-side transaction
by the persisted outbox row.

Publisher pump

OutboxPublisherBackgroundService runs in every hosting process
with the EventBus registered. On each tick:

S1-KUN-002（2026-10-09）修订：默认 EfOutboxMessageStore 在 PostgreSQL 事务里以 FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED 领取 Pending 且已到重试时间的消息，持有行锁直到本批次状态提交。broker 发布使用 confirms + mandatory；失败将指数退避时间保存至 NextAttemptAt，达到上限保持 Failed 供运维重放。

自定义非事务存储须显式配置分布式锁；Null 锁仅供明确单实例场景。数据库提交与 broker 确认不构成跨系统事务，确认后崩溃仍可能重放；消费者必须业务幂等。

Consumer idempotency

Publishing is at-least-once. Consumers IdempotentConsumerDecorator<T>
wraps every IIntegrationEventHandler<T>; first run writes the
stable event ID into IProcessedMessageStore (Redis
SETNX + EX keyed on {eventTypeId}:{eventId}). Subsequent
deliveries short-circuit before the handler body. See ADR trail
for Kun.EventBus.IntegrationEvent idempotency; this ADR only
states the contract: handlers must be safe to re-invoke and
the framework will make the decorator path cheap for them.

W3C trace propagation

OutboxMessage.TraceParent + TraceState capture
Activity.Current?.Id / TraceStateString at enqueue. The
publisher restores them on the outgoing envelope (traceparent
header) so the downstream consumer joins the original trace when
it starts its own activity via ActivitySource.StartActivity with
the parent id from the header.

Note — this is trace context propagation (W3C Trace Context
spec), not baggage propagation (ADR-013). Baggage is ambient
cross-cutting data (tenant / user / outbox-message-id)
deliberately mirrored onto spans and logs by the enricher; trace
context is just the trace ID chain. Kun keeps the two concepts
separate so that baggage can be audited / stripped at system
boundaries without affecting trace correlation.

Stable event IDs — format and registry

All integration events are tagged with a stable string identifier
"{bounded-context}.{name}.v{n}" — e.g. order.placed.v1,
billing.invoice.paid.v2. Two non-negotiables:

Never Type.AssemblyQualifiedName. Renaming a CLR type or
moving it across assemblies breaks every persisted row. The
stable ID is the wire contract.

Versioned suffix (v1, v2, …) is bumped on breaking payload
changes. Non-breaking additions (new optional property) keep
the version.

IEventTypeRegistry resolves eventTypeId ↔ CLR Type at runtime.
Consumers register via IEventTypeRegistrar in their DI
composition root; missing registrations fail loudly on publisher
startup rather than silently at publish time.

What Outbox does not do

Read-side projections / read models. Those belong in CQRS
Query handlers (Kun.Dapper). Outbox is the write-side egress.

Saga orchestration. Kun.Saga ADR-S01 is the orchestrator;
Saga steps use integration events for cross-service handoffs but
the orchestration state lives in its own table.

Command routing. Commands go through Kun.Mediator. Outbox
carries events only.

Snapshotting / rehydration. Outbox is for outgoing
messages. Inbound replay + aggregate rehydration is the read-
side concern.

Alternatives considered

Direct publish inside the handler

Rejected — either breaks atomicity (publish before commit) or
loses messages (publish after commit + crash). See §Context.

Change Data Capture (Debezium / Postgres logical replication)

Captures state changes, not semantic intents. You get row
changed messages; the consumer then has to reverse-engineer
"what business event happened?" Kun's integration events carry
semantics (OrderPlaced, not INSERT orders VALUES (…)), so a
CDC approach would need a translator layer that introduces the
same complexity as Outbox without its atomicity advantages.
Revisit only if an explicit data-lake / audit replay need appears.

Transactional outbox tables per-bounded-context

Each bounded context gets its own table. Considered, rejected —
no concrete benefit in the single-DB-per-service layout we run
today; one shared __outbox_messages__ table with
EventTypeId prefixing the bounded context is simpler and the
partial-index-on-Pending query cost is identical. Revisit if a
service needs per-context publishing priorities.

Kafka source + compacted topics as ledger

Moves the atomicity problem to the storage layer (Kafka-backed
state store). Operationally heavier than Postgres for the current
scale and mixes write-authority (DB) with event-authority (Kafka).
Deferred indefinitely.

Impact on existing code

None — this ADR is retroactive. The types described are the
types that have been shipping since Phase-1 M2. Cross-links to
this ADR land as part of KN-SELF-011 AC-2.

Follow-ups

F1: Dead-letter handling — Failed-status rows above retry
cap today sit in the table forever; needs a janitor job or a
dedicated DLQ table. Tracked as backlog item.

F2: Per-tenant batch priority — some tenants' events are
time-sensitive (webhook SLAs). Weight-based batch selection
sits outside the current ReadPendingBatchAsync.

F3: Outbox-specific test helpers in
Kun.Testing.EntityFrameworkCore (ADR-012 §F1 referenced this
as a companion module). **Resolved 2026-04-24 (KN-SELF-014
KN-SELF-016)** — shipped as a sibling module to
Kun.Testing with IsAotCandidate=false (matches
Kun.EntityFrameworkCore). Public surface is
OutboxAssertions with three helpers —
ShouldHaveOutboxMessage / ShouldHaveExactlyOneOutboxMessage /
ShouldNotHaveOutboxMessage — each offered as both an
extension on IEnumerable<OutboxMessage> (for tests that
pre-query a snapshot) and DbContext (for one-liner
assertions after SaveChangesAsync). All helpers throw
KunAssertionException with a mismatch message that includes
the helper name, expected EventTypeId, observed match
count, and the distinct EventTypeIds actually present.
Tests cover every helper × overload × pass/fail path
(11 tests; UseInMemoryDatabase for the DbContext
overload fixture). See also
docs/guides/validating-commands.md
for the validation-side sibling guide that KN-SELF-013
shipped.

事件契约包拆分（S1-KUN-010，2026-10-14）

IntegrationEventIdAttribute、IEventTypeRegistrar（含源生成 JsonTypeInfo<T> 重载）与 IEventTypeRegistry 迁入 Kun.EventBus.Abstractions，保持 Kun.EventBus 命名空间。该包只依赖 Kun.Core，不带 Redis、broker、DI 或宿主实现。Kun.EventBus 依赖新包并为迁移类型保留类型转发，现有注册表和 Outbox 行为不变。

IIntegrationEvent 原本定义于 Kun.Core.Domain，仍保留唯一类型；新抽象包通过传递依赖与类型转发导出它。这样契约包只引用新包即可声明事件，同时保持 Core 的根层地位、旧消费者的类型身份与源/二进制兼容性。

Change Data Capture (Debezium / Postgres logical replication)
Kafka source + compacted topics as ledger

title: ADR-016 配置可靠性、权限端口与能力目录
content:
本页镜像自 kun 仓库 docs/architecture/ADR-016-platform-ports.md（v2026.10.25）。Kun 文档与代码不一致处以代码为准（ADR-001 D1.8）；Qian 对 Kun 的选用与约束见与 Qian 的关系。改动请提到 kun 仓库。

状态：Accepted。日期：2026-10-09。执行依据：Qian 已接受的 ADR-006、ADR-007 与任务 S1-KUN-006；本文记录上游框架的落位，不引入新的权限模型。

决策

新增 Kun.Authorization 抽象包，仅定义主体、可解释判定、IPermissionChecker、IDataPermissionFilter、IFieldPolicy、命令静态权限声明与端点元数据，不提供 RBAC/ABAC 引擎或数据库实现。

HTTP 经 AddKunAuthorization() 与 RequireKunPermission() 接入 ASP.NET Core 策略；Mediator 命令实现 IPermissionProtectedRequest 并装配 AddPermissionBehavior，漏装时 Mediator 构建即拒绝（2026.10.13 起）；gRPC 的四种调用形态读取 [RequiresPermission] 元数据。缺少引擎一律拒绝，判定先于 handler 与流首帧读取。身份认证由已有 Security/Identity 入口提供；平台策略与权限管理属于下游。

Kun.Mediator 的 handler 注册可同时接收稳定能力 ID、请求和响应 JsonTypeInfo，经 ICapabilityRegistry 枚举 JSON Schema 2020-12。目录本身不等于调用授权；上层必须按权限与 scope 过滤后对外暴露。

AddKunOptions<T> 在变更后重新创建和校验候选值，成功才替换当前值；拒绝时保留旧对象并增加 kun.configuration.reload.rejected，日志不写配置内容。关键配置维持 ValidateOnStart，可选配置可延后至首次读取。Schema 导出表达 JSON 形状；DataAnnotations 与自定义语义校验仍由 validator 执行。

Kun.Configuration.Apollo 是独立 HTTP 配置源，支持 properties namespace 的有序叠加、长轮询、通知修订回传、AccessKey HMAC-SHA1、服务端故障转移与本地缓存。HMAC-SHA1 仅用于遵守 Apollo 既有协议，不用于新密码学设计。配置源不负责租户配置、secretRef 解析、发布审批或审计，这些由平台 Provider 负责。

KunExceptionHandler 通过 IProblemDetailsService 输出，让宿主可以安装自定义错误写入器。它不再绕过宿主直接序列化 ProblemDetails。

依赖与兼容

Kun.Authorization 只依赖 Kun.Core；Mediator、ASP.NET Core 与 gRPC 向下依赖它。Apollo provider 仅依赖标准 Configuration/Logging 抽象，无平台依赖。两包均开启 AOT 分析并加入 CI 发布矩阵。

旧仓储接口仍有兼容实现，不能删掉后假装从未使用：以 KUNLEGACY001 标记废弃，保留 EF 与旧存储内部兼容代码；新下游代码以 Banned API 门禁拒绝旧入口。新存储包是 Kun.Storage.Abstractions，其中接口的实际全名为 Kun.Storage.IFileStorage；旧 Kun.Storage 包中的接口是 Kun.Storage.Abstractions.IFileStorage。

AddKunDapper / AddKunDapperNpgsql 新增 Func<ReadDbOptions> 重载，解决 init-only 属性无法在 Action 内赋值，同时保留原方法二进制签名。慢请求阈值使用 PerformanceBehaviorOptions.ThresholdMs，原构造器和 500ms 默认值不变。

验证与边界

配置测试覆盖非法值、类型绑定错误、拒绝指标、有效修订恢复、可选配置、Schema 实例验证。Apollo 测试通过替身 HTTP 协议覆盖签名、缓存、鉴权失败不回退、离线启动失败、快照校验、长轮询修订回传；这是协议集成验收，未声明已对接生产 Apollo。

权限测试覆盖缺失引擎、明确拒绝与允许，以及 HTTP/Mediator/gRPC 判定顺序；错误处理中测试宿主写入器真正接管响应。没有在框架中实现租户 RBAC、字段脱敏算法或行级 SQL 编译器。
